body: The OSHA 300 Log is an official record used to track and document all work-related injuries and illnesses that meet OSHA’s recordable criteria. It’s one of the most important tools for maintaining compliance with U.S. workplace safety regulations and for ensuring that companies keep accurate, transparent safety records for every employee.
text:
Incidents > What is the OSHA 300 log for an employee?

The OSHA 300 Log is an official record used to track and document all work-related injuries and illnesses that meet OSHA’s recordable criteria. It’s one of the most important tools for maintaining compliance with U.S. workplace safety regulations and for ensuring that companies keep accurate, transparent safety records for every employee.
title: What is the OSHA 300 log for an employee?

heading: Purpose of the OSHA 300 Log
body:
The log helps employers and safety professionals:

- Monitor workplace safety trends and identify recurring hazards.
- Evaluate safety performance over time.
- Ensure compliance with OSHA’s injury and illness recordkeeping requirements (29 CFR 1904).
- Provide transparency for employees, auditors, and inspectors.
- Support preventive measures by analyzing where and why incidents occur.

- Evaluate safety performance over time.

- Provide transparency for employees, auditors, and inspectors.
- Support preventive measures by analyzing where and why incidents occur.
title: What is the OSHA 300 log for an employee?

heading: What It Records
body:
For each recordable case, the OSHA 300 Log includes details such as:

- Employee name and job title
- Date and location of the incident
- Description of the injury or illness
- Classification (e.g., days away from work, job transfer/restriction, or other recordable cases)
- Number of days the employee was away from work or on restricted duty
- Type of injury or illness (e.g., cut, sprain, respiratory condition, skin disorder, etc.)Each record must be specific to the employee and the event that occurred.

A T&M (Time & Materials) Invoice can be used when there is no fixed contract price, and the customer is billed based on the actual time spent and materials used for the project. The purpose of a T&M invoice is to gather the transactions, such as materials, labor hours and other expenses, over a specific period and bill them to the customer. To create a T&M invoice in Contractor Foreman, go to the Main Menu and select Invoices. Click the + Invoice button on the top right to create a new invoice. You will be prompted to fill in the information of the invoice and create it. After the invoice is created, go to the Items tab from the left panel of the invoice. Click on Add Item to Invoice, and a dropdown will appear. Select Add Time & Material Item from the options. A pop-up will appear, showing all available items that can be added to the invoice, such as:
Purchase Orders
Expenses
Change Orders
Time Cards
Bills
Equipment Logs

Select the relevant items you want to include in the invoice. After adding the T&M items to the invoice, you can set up a markup for each item if required. This allows you to charge an additional percentage on top of the cost for materials, labor, or any other expenses.

heading: Overview
body: When creating a Purchase Order in Contractor Foreman, you may notice two fields: Reference and FOB Point. These fields help provide additional context and clarity for tracking and managing material orders and deliveries.
text:
Purchase Orders > How is Reference & FOB point used in producing a Purchase Order? :: Overview

When creating a Purchase Order in Contractor Foreman, you may notice two fields: Reference and FOB Point. These fields help provide additional context and clarity for tracking and managing material orders and deliveries.
title: How is Reference & FOB point used in producing a Purchase Order?

heading: Reference Number
body:
The Reference Number field in a Purchase Order is used to tie the PO back to an external reference, such as:

- A Customer Purchase Order number
- A Delivery ticket
- A Warehouse pickup slipThis field serves as an additional layer of identification that connects your internal Purchase Order to a related external document or customer reference.

The Reference Number field in a Purchase Order is used to tie the PO back to an external reference, such as:

- A Customer Purchase Order number
- A Delivery ticket
- A Warehouse pickup slipThis field serves as an additional layer of identification that connects your internal Purchase Order to a related external document or customer reference.
title: How is Reference & FOB point used in producing a Purchase Order?

heading: FOB Point
body:
FOB (Free on Board) Point identifies the location where ownership and liability transfer from the supplier to the purchaser.
For example:

- If the FOB Point is the supplier’s warehouse, the purchaser assumes responsibility once the goods leave that location.
- If the FOB Point is the delivery destination, the supplier retains responsibility until the goods are received by the purchaser.This field helps clarify who is responsible for shipping costs, risks, and ownership at different stages of delivery.

body: In Contractor Foreman, you can link tasks between multiple projects in the Schedule Module. This ensures that if a task in one project is delayed, it will automatically trigger delays in related tasks in another project. This feature is especially useful for managing projects that rely on shared resources, subcontractors, or sequential workflows. To Link Tasks Across Multiple Projects, open the Schedule Module from the Main Menu. Click the “Select Project” button and choose the projects you want to manage together. Click Save to load them into the Gantt chart. Once selected, tasks from both projects will appear in the Gantt chart, allowing you to create relationships between them. To establish a relationship between tasks in different projects, identify the tasks you want to link. Locate the small circles (linking points) at each end of the task bars in the Gantt chart. The left circle represents the start of the task, and the right circle represents the end of the task. Click and drag from the end circle of one task to the start circle of another task. This creates a Finish-to-Start (FS) relationship, meaning the second task cannot begin until the first task is completed.

This feature is especially useful for managing projects that rely on shared resources, subcontractors, or sequential workflows. To Link Tasks Across Multiple Projects, open the Schedule Module from the Main Menu. Click the “Select Project” button and choose the projects you want to manage together. Click Save to load them into the Gantt chart. Once selected, tasks from both projects will appear in the Gantt chart, allowing you to create relationships between them. To establish a relationship between tasks in different projects, identify the tasks you want to link. Locate the small circles (linking points) at each end of the task bars in the Gantt chart. The left circle represents the start of the task, and the right circle represents the end of the task. Click and drag from the end circle of one task to the start circle of another task. This creates a Finish-to-Start (FS) relationship, meaning the second task cannot begin until the first task is completed.
title: How do I link tasks across multiple projects so if a task is delayed in one project it will trigger a delay in another project?

body:
Click and drag from the end circle of one task to the start circle of another task. This creates a Finish-to-Start (FS) relationship, meaning the second task cannot begin until the first task is completed. Once linked, any delay in the first task will push back the start of the dependent task. Understanding Relationship Types
You can create different types of relationships with tasks depending on how they should interact:
1. Finish-to-Start (FS) – Most Common
The second task cannot start until the first task is completed. Example: If “Foundation Work” in Project A is delayed, “Framing Work” in Project B will also be delayed. How to Set It Up: Connect the end circle of the first task to the start circle of the second task. 2. Start-to-Start (SS)
The second task cannot start until the first task has started. Example: “Excavation” in Project A must start as “Concrete Pouring” in Project B can begin. How to Set It Up: Connect the start circle of the first task to the start circle of the second task. 3. Finish-to-Finish (FF)
The second task cannot finish until the first task has finished.

In Contractor Foreman, you can send a Sub-Contract to a subcontractor for review and approval without requiring them to be a registered user of the software. - They will have an option to approve or reject the Sub-Contract based on the information provided. This is a streamlined and user-friendly process that ensures approval can be completed without needing to log in or be trained on the software.

body: The Type and Drawing fields in a Work Order are designed to serve as cross-references to your construction documents. These fields let you identify each Work Order directly to a sheet number or specific section of your construction plans.
text:
Work Orders > What is the purpose of the Type and Drawing fields in the Work Order?

The Type and Drawing fields in a Work Order are designed to serve as cross-references to your construction documents. These fields let you identify each Work Order directly to a sheet number or specific section of your construction plans.
title: What is the purpose of the Type and Drawing fields in the Work Order?

heading: Example
body: Imagine you’re working on a residential remodel and a Work Order is created to add new electrical outlets in the kitchen. By entering the corresponding Type (Electrical) and the Drawing (Sheet E-102), anyone reviewing the Work Order can quickly see the exact location and scope on the construction documents.

Imagine you’re working on a residential remodel and a Work Order is created to add new electrical outlets in the kitchen. By entering the corresponding Type (Electrical) and the Drawing (Sheet E-102), anyone reviewing the Work Order can quickly see the exact location and scope on the construction documents.
title: What is the purpose of the Type and Drawing fields in the Work Order?

heading: Why is this important?
body:
- Clarity: Ensures the field crew knows exactly where the work applies.
- Accountability: Reduces confusion between the customer, subcontractors, and your team.
- Efficiency: Saves time by minimizing back-and-forth communication—everyone can look at the same plan reference.
- Documentation: Keeps project records organized, especially when reviewing work after completion.
In short, the Type and Drawing fields help bridge the gap between project documentation and the tasks your team executes onsite.

What Types of Maintenance Are Tracked for Each Piece of Equipment
Purpose
To help you understand the full scope of maintenance data that Contractor Foreman allows you to track, record, and manage for each equipment asset logged in the system. Overview
Proper equipment maintenance tracking is essential for extending the life of your assets, ensuring job site safety, and reducing costly breakdowns. Contractor Foreman’s Equipment Logs enable field operators and office staff to maintain a comprehensive digital history of each machine’s usage, inspections, and service needs. Each log entry contributes to a running history of maintenance and operational activity. Below is a detailed breakdown of each maintenance-related field tracked. Tracked Maintenance Categories

1. Beginning Hours / Ending Hours

- These fields represent the meter readings at the start and end of the equipment usage period for the day.
- Purpose: Captures the duration of daily use.
- Where to enter: In the Equipment Log details view.
- Example: Beginning = 1,250 hrs; Ending = 1,265 hrs. 2.

Beginning Hours / Ending Hours

- These fields represent the meter readings at the start and end of the equipment usage period for the day.
- Purpose: Captures the duration of daily use.
- Where to enter: In the Equipment Log details view.
- Example: Beginning = 1,250 hrs; Ending = 1,265 hrs. 2. Total Hours

- Auto-calculated by the system as:
Ending Hours – Beginning Hours
- Purpose: Used to track wear and service intervals.
- Can be referenced in:

Maintenance schedules
Cost tracking
Utilization reports
3. Fuel (Gallons) Added

- Manual entry field to document the amount of fuel added during or after usage.
- Purpose: Tracks fuel consumption rates and refueling history.
- Also useful for reconciling project-level fuel costs. 4. Water Inspected

- Use this to confirm that the cooling system and water levels were inspected.
- Why it matters: Overheating can damage engines—checking coolant levels helps prevent this. 5. Lube Inspected

- Indicates whether lubrication points or grease fittings were checked.
- Purpose: Proper lubrication prevents mechanical wear and helps extend component life. 6.

body: The “Variation” field in Contractor Foreman allows users to manage different product variations within a single cost item, such as variations in color or style, without needing to create multiple separate items for each variation. This is particularly useful for items that share a base price but differ in specific details. To set up variations for an item, navigate to the Cost Items Database by going to the Menu. If you need to create a new item, depending on the item type you need to add, go to the relevant tab. For example, if you want to add a material item, go to the material tab, and click the drop-down menu in the top right named “Select Option for Material Item”. Then click Add Material. Alternatively, to edit an existing item, find the item in the list, click on the green pencil icon to open the item details, and begin editing. Within the item details, you will see a field labeled Variations. This is where you can add different versions of the same item. For example, if you’re adding a paint item with different color options, you can input the variations as “Red,” “Blue,” “Green,” etc. Simply type the name of the variation in the Variation field and press Enter.

title: How do I use the “variation” field within the Cost Items Database and Estimate?

body: For example, if you’re adding a paint item with different color options, you can input the variations as “Red,” “Blue,” “Green,” etc. Simply type the name of the variation in the Variation field and press Enter. This will add the variation to the item. Repeat this process for each variation you want to include. Once you’ve added all the necessary variations, save the item. Your item will now include these variations in the Cost Items Database. Once the item with variations has been added to the Cost Items Database, you can use it within an estimate. Here’s how to select a variation when creating or editing an estimate. Navigate to the Estimates module, and either create a new estimate or open an existing one. Click here to see how to create an estimate and how to add items to the estimate. In the Items tab of the estimate, import the cost item from the cost items database to the relevant section. After adding the item to the estimate, click on the preview button to the right of the line item to open its details. Here, you will find the variations field that allows you to select one of the variations you added earlier (e.g., different colors or sizes).

heading: Why Is This Important?
body: Adding marketing activities to your calendar helps you track leads, follow-ups, and client interactions in one centralized place. Since you can create these tasks from almost any module, you can capture opportunities instantly — without switching screens. This improves team coordination, time management, and accountability, ensuring that no opportunity is ever missed.
text:
Calendar > How can I add a Marketing activity to my Calendar? :: Why Is This Important?

Adding marketing activities to your calendar helps you track leads, follow-ups, and client interactions in one centralized place. Since you can create these tasks from almost any module, you can capture opportunities instantly — without switching screens. This improves team coordination, time management, and accountability, ensuring that no opportunity is ever missed.
title: How can I add a Marketing activity to my Calendar?

heading: Option 1
body:
You can add a Marketing Activity (or any sales-related task) from almost anywhere within Contractor Foreman. This flexibility allows you to stay productive and organized no matter where you are in the platform.
Here’s how to do it:

- Click the “+ Task” button located at the bottom right corner of the screen (as shown in the screenshot below).
- A pop-up window will appear on the right side of the screen .
- In the Task Type field, select Sales Task .
- Fill in all the required details — such as title, due date, description, and assigned employee.
- Once complete, click Save .
That’s it! The task will now appear in the Calendar of the person it was assigned to.
Alternative Option
You can also add a marketing activity directly from within a Lead or Opportunity.
To do this, open the Lead or Opportunity record and add a Task related to it. When you create the task this way, it will automatically be added as a Sales Activity linked to that specific Lead or Opportunity.
To learn more about this process, please refer to the articles:

- Leads Module
- Opportunities Module

When you open a Change Order record, you will see a set of circles with different Stages or Status at the top of the page. These stages represent different statuses that a Change Order can have throughout its lifecycle, such as “On Hold”, “Open”, “Pending Approval”, “Unbilled/Approved”, and “Billed”. These stages will automatically update when you perform certain actions:

- When you submit the Change Order to the Customer, the status of the Change Order will go from “On-Hold” or “Open” to “Pending Approval”
- When the customers receives and approves (signs electronically) the Change Order, the Status of the Change Order will change or move to “Unbilled/Approved”
- When you generate an Invoice, and you import (use) the Change Order items at 100% from the SOV, then you submit the invoice to the Customer, at this point in time is when the Change Order will change its status to Billed.To manually change the Change Order status from “On Hold” to “Billed,” click on the “Billed” circle.

Tracking task completion in the Schedule Module of Contractor Foreman is essential for monitoring project progress. You can update task progress in two ways: by manually entering a percentage in the task details or by adjusting progress directly on the Gantt chart. 1. Updating Task Progress from the Task Details
Open the Schedule Module from the Main Menu. Locate the task you want to update. Double-click on the task name or task bar to open the task details. Find the “Progress” dropdown field. Enter the percentage of completion manually or select from the provided list. Click Save to apply the update. This method allows you to record the completion percentage for each task precisely. 2. Updating Task Progress from the Gantt Chart
Open the Schedule Module and select your project. Place your mouse cursor over the task bar in the Gantt chart. Locate the small triangle at the start of the progress bar. Click and drag the triangle to update the task’s percentage completion. also update the progress as manually updating, making it easier to see how a task is advancing in real-time.

Effective project management relies heavily on accurate tracking of submittals throughout their lifecycle, from initial creation to final approval. The Submittals Module in Contractor Foreman offers a centralized location where all project-related submittals can be monitored, filtered, and reviewed in real time.
Whether you need to check the current status of a pending approval, verify who a submittal is assigned to, or confirm deadlines, this module provides the necessary visibility and control to stay organized and on schedule.

heading: Access the Submittals Module
body:
Begin by navigating to the Submittals section of the system. This is where all existing submittals are listed and where the copy functionality is accessed.
●From the main navigation menu, follow this path:

○Menu > Submittals

●This opens the Submittals dashboard, where you can see a list of all submittals previously entered for the current project.
Why this matters: Centralizing submittals in one location helps project teams quickly assess progress, spot bottlenecks, and ensure compliance with required documentation workflows.

heading: View the List of Submittals
body:
Once in the Submittals module, you’ll see a full list of all submittals associated with your projects. Each row in the list view includes multiple columns that provide at-a-glance insights. These include:
●Submittal Number:
A unique identifier automatically or manually assigned to the submittal. This number helps with reference and retrieval in logs, reports, and communications.

●Title:
The name or brief description of the submittal
●Project:
The specific project the submittal is associated with

●Status:
Displays the current stage of the submittal workflow. Common statuses include:

○Draft – Created but not yet submitted.

○Submitted – Sent for review or approval.

○Approved – Fully reviewed and accepted.

○Rejected – Requires revisions or has been denied.

○Revise & Resubmit – Needs changes before approval can be granted.

●Tracking status helps you monitor where each submittal stands and take action when required.

●Due Date:
The deadline by which the submittal must be reviewed or approved. This is critical for time-sensitive materials or components that impact the construction schedule.

heading: Use Filters or Search to Narrow Results
body:
When managing dozens, or even hundreds, of submittals across multiple projects, finding a specific one can be time-consuming. To streamline your workflow:
●Use the Search Bar at the top of the Submittals Dashboard to search by:

○Submittal number

○Title

○Project name

○Assigned user

●Use the Filters to narrow the list by:

○Status (e.g., show only “Revise & Resubmit” or “Draft” submittals)

○Project

○Due Date

○Assigned Reviewer

Best Practice: Use filters during weekly coordination meetings or quality control checks to quickly surface outstanding or overdue submittals and assign follow-up tasks.

heading: When to Use Bills
body:
Use Bills for quantified, planned purchases tied to the project estimate. These typically come from vendors (via Purchase Orders) or subcontractors (via Subcontracts).

Examples include:

- 10 cubic yards of concrete.
- Furnish and Install 15 windows.
- 500 square feet of vinyl plank flooring.

heading: When to Use Expenses
body:
Use Expenses for incidental or unplanned costs that are not explicitly listed in the project estimate. These are often smaller, immediate purchases needed to keep the project running smoothly.

Examples include:

- Fuel for equipment.
- Replacing a broken tool.
- Buying lunch for the crew.

heading: Impact on Job Costing
body:
Bills: Since they relate to estimated and planned items, Bills directly affect the budgeted costs and help track whether the project stays within the planned budget according the use of Cost Codes in your Project. They can be associated typically to Material, Equipment and Subcontractor items.
Expenses: These capture the unplanned costs, providing a complete picture of actual spending. They help identify areas where additional funds are being used, mapping this cost with the use of Cost Codes, enabling better forecasting and management for future projects.They can be associated to any item type.
Clear distinction and proper categorization ensure accurate job costing, improved budgeting, and better financial oversight in residential construction.

Cross-referencing incident or accident logs with daily logs provides a comprehensive view of site conditions and activities surrounding the event. This correlation helps identify contributing factors, such as weather, personnel on-site, or equipment used, allowing for more accurate root cause analysis. It also strengthens documentation for liability, insurance claims, and future preventive measures, enhancing safety protocols and accountability on the jobsite.
When you create an incident in the Incidents Module, this incident or accident is visible in the details section of the Daily Log.

To effectively track the work performed by a 1099 subcontractor, use time cards to log the hours they work. This provides a clear record of the time spent on the job and helps you monitor labor costs and productivity. You can then run a report that shows all the hours put by this subcontractor. This not only protects both parties in case of disputes but also helps the subcontractor demonstrate the value of their work to future clients or during audits.

heading: How do I move files from one folder to another within Files and Photos?
body:
To move files between folders in the Files and Photos module, follow these steps:

- Go to the main menu and open the Files and Photos module.
- Locate the project where your files are stored. On the left-hand side of the screen, you’ll see a list of all your projects. Click on the project of your interest.
- Once inside the project, open the folder that contains the file(s) you want to move.
- Hover over the file and click the checkbox in the top left corner of the file preview.
- After selecting one or multiple files, several action buttons will appear at the top of the screen.
- On the right-hand side, click the Move icon or button.
- Choose the destination folder where you want to move your file(s), and confirm the action.
Important: You can only move files that were uploaded directly into the Files and Photos module or into a Project folder.
Files that are linked to specific records (such as Submittals, Daily Logs, RFIs, etc.) cannot be moved. This is because those files are tied to the record where they were originally uploaded.

In Contractor Foreman, the option to import items from an Estimate into a Change Order exists to simplify and streamline the process of creating accurate Change Orders, especially when the items related to the Change Order have already been detailed in the original Estimate, users can save time and reduce errors by importing these items directly into the Change Order. This prevents the need to recreate each item from scratch manually, ensuring that all details such as unit costs and descriptions are consistent with the original project Estimate.
While importing from an Estimate is a useful tool, it is not mandatory. Users have the flexibility to add items manually or adjust them as needed, allowing for a fully customized Change Order. This option gives project managers the freedom to handle different situations, whether they are dealing with predefined work from the Estimate or entirely new tasks that have come up during the project.

body: Tracking labor costs is essential for managing a project’s financial health, even when cost codes are not being used in timecards. While cost codes can provide detailed job costing, Contractor Foreman still allows labor to be tracked and reflected in the project without cost codes. Labor cost is determined by calculating the labor cost based on the employee’s wage, burden, or billing rate, along with the preferences set in the project module settings (Financials). When cost codes are not being used, labor is tracked as a unassigned cost. When you navigate to the Reports section of a project, you can see costs recorded by time cards categorized using cost codes if you use appropriate cost codes when you use time cards. But if you do not use cost codes, all costs recorded by time cards will be listed as Unassigned in the reports section. Labor costs are calculated based on the hourly rate of the employee or contractor who is recording time. These rates can be configured in the employee profile, and the calculation method can be set in the project module settings.

heading: Configuring Labor Cost Calculation Preferences
body:
While the Time tab displays the labor costs based on the timecards, it’s important to ensure that the correct rates are being applied to those entries. To configure labor cost calculation preferences, go to the Projects module and click on the gear icon to access the Project Module Settings. Under General Settings, you can configure how labor costs are calculated for the project. In the section labeled Job Cost Report: Labor Calculations, you can choose from the following options:
Approved Estimate: Labor costs will be calculated based on the rates used in the project’s approved estimate. Wage Rate: Labor costs will be calculated using the wage rate set in each employee or contractor’s profile. Burden Rate: This includes additional costs such as worker’s compensation, insurance and benefits on top of the employee’s wage rate. Billing Rate: Labor costs will be calculated using the billing rate, which it is the actual cost of the cost of the employee per hour plus profit. Make sure that the correct option is selected based on how you want to calculate labor costs for the project.

body:
Purpose
Adding a video link to your Safety Meetings is a simple but powerful way to reinforce safety procedures, demonstrate best practices, or meet OSHA and internal training requirements. Whether it’s a third-party training video or company-produced walkthrough, linking to video content helps improve clarity and engagement during safety discussions. When Should You Use This?

- To visually demonstrate procedures that are difficult to explain in text
- To support a toolbox, talk or safety topic with relevant real-world examples
- To meet industry compliance standards that require multimedia training
- When introducing a new process or tool to your crew
Steps to Add a Video Link to a Safety Meeting

- Navigate to the Main Menu
- Click on Safety Meetings

- From the list view, select the Safety Meeting where you want to add a video

- Once inside the selected Safety Meeting, look to the left-side panel and click on Notes

- In the Notes section, click on the Note tab

- Click Add Attachment

- In the pop-up window:

Choose Video as the attachment type
Paste the video link (e.g., YouTube, Vimeo, or company-hosted video)
Enter a Title (e.g., “Ladder Safety Overview”)
Add a brief Description explaining what the video covers or why it’s important
- Click Submit to save the video to the Safety Meeting
What to Keep in Mind

- The video will now be accessible within the meeting record and can be viewed during or after the meeting
- Only users with appropriate permissions (Admin or Full Access) can add video attachments
- Be sure the video link is publicly accessible or shared properly if it’s a private/internal link
- Videos can help document that your meeting content included visual training components, which may support compliance reviews

body: Sometimes, a single contact may have multiple people associated with it, such as when you’re working with a customer who has other individuals that are important to the project. In these cases, you can add Additional Contacts to the main contact’s record. This feature is especially helpful when multiple people need access to the client portal. To begin, go to the Directory module, where all your contacts are listed. This can be found in the main menu of Contractor Foreman. From the list of contacts, click on the specific contact to which you want to add additional contacts. This could be a lead, customer, contractor, or a vendor. Once you click on a contact, you will be taken to that contact’s profile page. On the profile page, look for the Additional Contacts widget. This widget will allow you to manage any additional contacts related to the primary contact. Click the +Additional Contact button within the widget. This will open a form where you can input the details of the new additional contact. Fill in the necessary details for the additional contact and click Save. The new contact will now appear in the Additional Contacts widget under the primary contact’s profile.

heading: Cleaning vs. Adding Punch List Items
body:
- Cleaning a punch list means addressing and marking existing items as complete.
- Adding items means recognizing new deficiencies and including them for correction.Both are equally important: one ensures the original issues are resolved, while the other ensures any new issues don’t slip through the cracks.

By continuously updating your punch list, you demonstrate that quality control is an active process—not just a final checklist. It helps you deliver projects that meet or exceed expectations, building trust with owners, inspectors, and your own team.

body:
To add a new tax rate: On the right side of the Tax Rates section, click the Add Tax Rate + button. A new window or form will appear, allowing you to input the details of your new tax rate. In the form for adding a new tax rate, you can add your tax rates as a single tax rate or a combined tax rate. Select the suitable type, and you’ll need to provide specific details such as:

- Tax Name: Give the tax rate a name that clearly identifies it, such as “State Sales Tax” or “VAT”.
- Tax Percentage: Enter the percentage value for the tax. For example, if your sales tax is 10%, input “10%.”

Your new tax rate will now be available for selection when creating estimates, invoices, and other financial documents in Contractor Foreman.

Archiving an estimate is a useful way to keep your active estimates list organized by moving estimates that are no longer in use to the archived section.
Method 1: Archiving an Estimate from the List View
Navigate to the Estimates Module from the Main Menu. Once you are in the Estimates module, you will see the list of all the estimates you have created. Scroll through the list of estimates and find the one you wish to archive. To the right of each estimate in the list, you will see three vertical dots. Click on these dots to open additional options.

From the drop-down options, click on Archive. This will archive the estimate, removing it from the active estimates list.
Method 2: Archiving an Estimate from the Estimate Details Page
Instead of archiving the estimate from the list view, you can also archive it from within the estimate. First, open the estimate you want to archive by clicking on its name in the estimates list. Once the estimate is open, click the three dots to the top right corner of the estimate page. In the drop-down menu, select the Archive option.

Even after archiving an estimate, you can always retrieve it later if necessary.

In the Opportunity record, use the Sales Rep field to assign the Opportunity to a specific employee. This makes them the owner of that Opportunity, meaning they are responsible for managing it and everything related to it. When assigned, the employee will receive a one-time notification informing them that a new Opportunity has been assigned. 2. Create a Task linked to the Opportunity:
For more flexibility and ongoing reminders, you can create a Task within the Opportunity and assign it to the employee. This option allows you to specify actions or deadlines for follow-up. The assigned employee will receive a push notification in the mobile app, a text message (if enabled and located in the U.S.), and an email notification—ensuring they don’t miss the follow-up. This second method is especially effective for keeping follow-ups consistent and visible across your team.
title: How do I notify or assign an Opportunity to an Employee for follow-up?

How to Attach a File or Image to a Safety Meeting
Purpose
Attaching files or images to a Safety Meeting record allows you to document real-time jobsite safety, enhance accountability, and provide visual proof of compliance. Whether it’s a sign-in sheet, photos of PPE usage, or site-specific hazards—attaching files ensures your safety documentation is clear, complete, and easily accessible for audits or internal tracking. When You Might Want to Attach Files or Photos

- A picture of the sign-in sheet from the meeting
- A photo of all attendees gathered during the talk
- Images of the hazard or equipment being discussed
- A PDF handout used during the meeting
- Reference materials, checklists, or even site mapsAttachments can help demonstrate that a meeting took place, what was discussed, and what conditions were present—all useful for OSHA audits or internal investigations.

body:

- A photo of all attendees gathered during the talk

- Reference materials, checklists, or even site mapsAttachments can help demonstrate that a meeting took place, what was discussed, and what conditions were present—all useful for OSHA audits or internal investigations. Steps to Attach a File or Image to a Safety Meeting

- Navigate to the Main Menu
- Select Safety Meetings from the list

- From the list view, find the meeting you want to update

You can use the search bar or filters to quickly find it

- Click on the meeting title to open it
- Once inside the meeting record, click the Files button on the left side of the page

- Click the Add Attachment button

- Click on the “Add an Attachment” button

A window will pop up allowing you to upload files or images from your device
On a mobile device or tablet , this may also open your camera directly , so you can snap and attach live photos instantly

- Choose the file(s) or photo(s) you’d like to add
- Once selected, the file(s) will appear in the list under the Safety Meeting record
- Click “Submit” at the bottom to save your changes

Additional Notes

- You can attach multiple files if needed
- Most common formats are supported (.JPG, .PNG, .PDF, .DOC, etc.)
- Attached files stay stored with the meeting record and are visible to anyone with access to the meeting
- If you need to remove or replace an attachment, just use the trash/delete icon next to it before submitting your updates
Why It Matters
Keeping proper documentation isn’t just about checking boxes—it protects your company, improves jobsite communication, and reinforces a culture of safety.

When importing cost codes from a CSV file into Contractor Foreman, it’s important to avoid creating duplicate cost codes that could lead to confusion or disorganization within your system. Contractor Foreman has built-in features to prevent exact duplicates from being imported. However, it’s always good to follow a few steps to ensure smooth importing and accurate management of your cost codes. How Contractor Foreman Handles Duplicate Cost Codes
Exact Matches Not Imported: If a cost code already exists in your system with the exact parent code and child code numbering, it will not be re-imported from the CSV file. But if the parent code is different, or the child code number varies (even slightly), and it doesn’t already exist under that specific parent code, the system will treat it as a new entry and import it. Steps to Avoid Duplicate Cost Codes
Export Your Current Cost Codes List: Before importing a new CSV file, first export your existing cost codes to ensure you have a reference of what’s already in the system. Go to Settings and then to the Cost Codes section. Click the Action button in the upper left corner of the screen and select Export Cost Codes.

body:

Export Your Current Cost Codes List: Before importing a new CSV file, first export your existing cost codes to ensure you have a reference of what’s already in the system. Go to Settings and then to the Cost Codes section. Click the Action button in the upper left corner of the screen and select Export Cost Codes. This will download a CSV file of your current cost codes. Adjust and Review Your New List: Open the exported CSV file and compare it with your new list of cost codes that you intend to import. If you find any cost codes that already exist, you can remove them from your new list to avoid importing duplicates. Import the Adjusted List: Once you’ve reviewed and adjusted your list, you can proceed with importing it. Ensure the file follows the correct CSV template format for cost code imports in Contractor Foreman. To import, go to Settings > Cost Codes, click the Action button, and select Import Cost Codes (From File). Important Notes
Used Cost Codes Cannot Be Deleted: Once a cost code has been used in any module of Contractor Foreman, it cannot be deleted. However, you can archive it if it’s no longer needed.

body: In Contractor Foreman, awarding a bid that has been received via a bid package allows you to finalize which vendor or contractor will be responsible for performing the work associated with that estimate. To award a bid package, first, navigate to the Estimates Module the Main Menu. Click on the bidding tab, located on the left panel. Then click on the eyeball icon to open the bid package. Once you have opened the bid package click on the Submissions tab on the left panel. This will take you to the screen where you can award the best bidder. For each bidder listed, there is a drop-down menu below their name. Find the bidder you wish to award the bid to, and click on the drop-down menu below their name. Select Awarded from the list of options. Once you’ve selected the bidder you want to award, click Save to confirm and apply your changes. This will officially award the bid to the chosen bidder and Contractor Foreman will ask you if you want to update the price of the items based on the bid provided by the bidders. After the above question, another question will pop up asking if you would you like to send an email to the winning bidder as well as those who lost the bid?

When working with Bills in Contractor Foreman, you may want to customize how information is displayed in the PDF format. While the templates are not fully customizable, you do have control over several display options and layout settings through the Templates settings. Here’s how you can make these adjustments safely and effectively. Navigate to Template Settings
To begin, go to the Main Menu and go to Settings. Within Settings, look for and select Templates. This is where all document formats—such as Invoices, Estimates, Change Orders, and Bills—are stored and managed. Select the “Bills” Template Type
Once inside the Templates settings, use the drop-down menu in the top-right corner to select Bills. This filters the templates so you’re only working with those that relate specifically to Bills. Choose Template
Select the Bill template that you’d like to modify. Before making any changes, it is strongly recommended to click the Copy icon (which looks like two stacked sheets of paper). This creates a duplicate version of the template. Why copy first? Making changes to the copied version ensures that your original template remains untouched.

body:
Before making any changes, it is strongly recommended to click the Copy icon (which looks like two stacked sheets of paper). This creates a duplicate version of the template. Why copy first? Making changes to the copied version ensures that your original template remains untouched. If something goes wrong during editing, you’ll always have the original template to fall back on. Edit the Copied Template
Click on the edit button (green pencil) of the copied version of the template to start editing it. You will see a series of options that allow you to:

- Turn sections on or off (e.g., vendor address, item descriptions, totals).
- Rearrange sections by moving them up or down. Use 3 horizontal lines of the sections and items to rearrange them. While full field customization (like renaming field and section names) may not be possible, these adjustments still allow you to create a clean, professional layout that fits your specific documentation needs. Set as Default: Once you’re happy with the layout and settings, you can set your new template as the default for future bills.

Changing the Ship to Address on a Purchase Order
Purpose
Updating the Ship To address on a Purchase Order is essential to ensure that materials, equipment, and supplies arrive at the correct location. This avoids costly delivery errors, project delays, and logistical confusion. Whether the delivery location changes due to evolving project needs, administrative corrections, or vendor instructions, timely updates keep procurement and fulfillment aligned. When to Update the Ship to Address
You should update the shipping address when:

- The delivery location changes after the PO was initially created. For example, materials originally ordered to a warehouse now need to be sent directly to the jobsite.
- The original Ship To address was incorrect , outdated, or incomplete.
- The vendor requests shipping to a different address due to logistical reasons, such as delivering to a satellite office or staging area.
- The PO is for owner-furnished materials that need to be sent directly to the client’s site.
- You need to pause shipment temporarily by putting the order on hold. Step-by-Step Instructions

- Click the drop-down menu next to the Ship To label.
- You will see several standard shipping options available. Choose the one that best fits your delivery needs:
Shipping Address Options Explained

- Company Address:
Your organization’s primary office, warehouse, or distribution center. Use When: Deliveries are to be received centrally and redistributed later.
- Pickup Address:
A designated location, often a vendor warehouse or supplier lot, where your team or vendor will pick up materials. Use When: Coordinating local pickups or will-call services where the supplier holds items for you to collect.
- Project Address:
The physical jobsite tied to the specific project associated with the PO. Use When: Direct-to-site delivery is required for materials, equipment, or labor to be used immediately at the work location.
- Hold:
Indicates the shipment should be paused or delayed until further notice. The vendor should not ship until cleared.

To convert an Opportunity into a Project, open the Opportunity record and click on the three-dot (⋮) icon located at the top right corner of the screen. From the dropdown menu, select “Create Project.”
Once you do this, the Opportunity will automatically be converted into a Project and will no longer appear under the Opportunities module, since it is now an active Project.
If the Opportunity was originally linked to a Lead, that Lead will also be converted into a Customer and will now appear in the Directory under Customers, instead of under the Leads tab.
Everything associated with the Opportunity—such as estimates, files, and notes—will be transferred to the new Project, ensuring that no information is lost in the conversion process.

In Contractor Foreman, copying a section and its items is a convenient way to duplicate an entire set of line items within an estimate, saving time and ensuring consistency.
Navigate to the Estimates Module from the Main Menu; select the Estimates module. From the list of estimates, pick the estimate in which you would like to copy a section. Click on the estimate to open it.
Once the estimate is open, navigate to the Items tab located in the left-hand panel. This tab will display all the sections and line items within the selected estimate.

Find the section with the items you wish to copy. Next to the section name to the right, locate the Add Items/Modify Section drop-down menu. Click on this drop-down menu to view available options.

From the drop-down options, select Copy Section.
This will duplicate the entire section, including all its line items. You can then rename the section, make any necessary adjustments, and proceed with further modifications if needed.

heading: Why is this useful?
body:
Contractor Foreman does not currently offer formal “inspection templates.” However, by copying inspections, you can create your own workflow that works like a template system:

- Repeatability : If you always run the same type of inspections (e.g., “Rebar Inspection” or “Waterproofing Inspection”), you can create one fully detailed inspection with all the items and checklists you typically use, and then copy it for every new project.
- Efficiency : Instead of entering the same details again and again, you only update what’s unique to the new project (such as date, assigned person, or inspector’s name).
- Consistency : Your team gets inspections that look and feel the same every time, reducing the chances of forgetting important checklist items.
- Field-ready templates : By pre-building inspections and copying them, you’re essentially creating a library of “inspection templates” for your field managers and staff to use—making their job easier and more consistent.Knowing how to copy inspections is one of the best time-saving strategies in Contractor Foreman, especially since it doubles as a custom template system for your company.

body:
Duplicating an existing submittal can be a helpful time-saving feature, particularly when managing repetitive processes, submitting similar materials across different phases, or following a standardized format. Rather than building a new submittal from scratch, Contractor Foreman offers a convenient method to create a copy of any previously created submittal.
This process is useful when:
●You’re submitting the same or a slightly modified product for another area or floor.

●You need to follow a similar review workflow for a comparable component.

●You want to retain formatting, structure, and documentation used in an earlier submittal.

body:

heading: Locate and Open the Submittal to Be Copied
body:
Once you’re in the Submittals module, scroll through the list or use filters/search to find the specific submittal you wish to duplicate.
●When you’ve identified the correct entry, click the three vertical dots (“⋮”) on the far right of the row.

●A small dropdown menu will appear with available options related to that specific submittal.

●Select the option labeled “Copy” (or similar, depending on the system version).

Tip: Look for submittals that closely match the new one you’re planning to submit. The closer the original is to your needs, the less editing you’ll need to do afterward.

heading: Confirm Copy Action
body:
After selecting the copy option:
●A system prompt will appear, asking you to confirm your action.

●Click “Yes” to proceed.

The system will now generate a duplicate of the original submittal. This copied version will typically include:
●All item details (names, descriptions, item numbers, etc.)

●Attached documents (cut sheets, drawings, files, etc.)

●Status and metadata (you may need to manually update these)

Reminder: The duplicated submittal is saved as a new, editable draft. The original remains unchanged.

heading: Review and Update the Copied Submittal
body:
After the copy is created, it’s important to review and revise the new submittal to suit its new purpose.
●Update the submittal title, item numbers, or product names if applicable.

●Replace or remove files that aren’t relevant to the new instance.

●Adjust spec sections, drawing numbers, or manufacturers as needed.

●Review external response sections, if copied over, and clear them if starting a new review cycle.

body: Creating a default Scope of Work for your estimates in Contractor Foreman allows you to streamline the estimate creation process, ensuring that you have a pre-defined set of work items ready for every new estimate. This eliminates the need to manually enter the scope of work each time, saving time and reducing the risk of missing important scope of work items. To begin, go to the Main Menu and select the Estimates module. This module is where you can manage all of your project estimates and related bid activities. Once you’re inside the Estimates module, click on the gear icon located in the top-right corner of the screen. This will open the Settings for the Estimates module, allowing you to customize various aspects, including the Scope of Work. Within the General Settings section of the Estimates Settings, you will see a field called Estimates (Scope of Work). This is where you can create your default Scope of Work list. Click the green pencil icon to the top right of the settings window to go to the edit mode of the settings. In Edit mode, you can start adding the specific scope of work items that you want to appear by default in all of your future estimates.

title: How do I create a default Scope of Work for an Estimate?

body: Click the green pencil icon to the top right of the settings window to go to the edit mode of the settings. In Edit mode, you can start adding the specific scope of work items that you want to appear by default in all of your future estimates. Enter each item as part of a list, making sure to include every aspect of work that is common across your projects. Once you have added all of your scope of work items, click Save to finalize your changes. This list will now serve as the default Scope of Work for all future estimates. heading: How to create your own Forms and Checklists?
body:
You can create your own Forms and Checklists within Contractor Foreman using the two form builders we offer, which are the Basic Form Builder and the Advanced Form Builder.
To get started, click on the + New Form button on the top right of the Forms and Checklists module. When you click that button, it will prompt you to select a form builder by either choosing the Basic Form Builder or the Advanced Form Builder.

Basic Form Builder: Ideal for simple checklists or forms with a few fields. This option is quicker and easier to use if you’re looking to build straightforward forms. Click here to see how to create a form using the Basic Form Builder.
Advanced Form Builder: Offers more flexibility and customization options, allowing you to create detailed, multi-section forms with a variety of field types and custom layouts. Click here to see how to create a form using the Advanced Form Builder.

heading: How to create a form using the Basic Form Builder?
body: When you click on the + New Form button and select the Basic Form Builder, the system will take you to the form builder where you can create your own form. You will see three fields on the top where you can set key information about the form. Status: While you are in the process of creating the process, you can set the status as “Do Not Use”. You can make edits, save the form, and make edits later until you publish the form to use. Once you finalize everything, set the status as “Published:Ready to Use” and you will be able to use that form under your company forms. Form Name: Set a name for your form here. This is the name which will be displayed under your company forms once you publish it. Notes: Any notes you want to save related to the form can be entered here. These notes will not be visible to the person who is filling out the form. It will only be visible whenever you edit the form. Just under those fields, you will see a checkbox called “Require signature when Submitting form”. If you enable it, the person who will fill out the form will be prompted to sign the form while submitting. Below all of those, you will see a box on the left side. This is where you can build your form.

heading: Key Differences: Field Types and Functionalities
body:
While the Basic Form Builder allows you to include standard fields like text boxes, checkboxes, and select dropdowns, the Advanced Form Builder expands your options to include the following additional field types:
Customer Multiple: Allows the form user to select multiple customers from the customer list. Employee Multiple: Enables selection of multiple employees from the employee list. Contractor Multiple: Enables selection of multiple contractors from the contractor list. Customer & Lead Multiple: This field allows selecting both customers and leads, and can be used in cases where either is relevant. Dropdown: Similar to the Select field but with enhanced options for dropdown menus, providing more flexibility. Comment: Add a field for users to leave comments or detailed responses. Rating: Useful for rating systems, such as a satisfaction survey where the user can select a rating (e.g., 1-5 stars). Image Picker: This is a question type that displays multiple images or videos and allows users to select one or more items. Boolean: A simple Yes/No toggle field. HTML: For advanced users, the HTML field allows you to add HTML content directly into your form for custom designs or instructions.

heading: Advanced Functionalities: “Enable if” and “Visible if”
body:
The Advanced Form Builder provides powerful functionalities that help you create dynamic forms based on user inputs. Two key features are:
Enable If: This feature allows you to control when a particular field becomes active (i.e., when the user is allowed to interact with it). For example, you may want a field to become enabled only if the user selects a particular option in a previous question.
Visible If: Similar to “Enable if,” this feature controls when a field is visible to the user. You can hide certain fields unless certain conditions are met, streamlining the user experience and making your forms more efficient.

Both of these functionalities can be found when editing a field. When you click on the Edit button of any form field, you’ll see these options in the advanced settings section, allowing you to set conditions that trigger visibility or enablement based on previous answers.

heading: Example: Creating a Conditional Form with Advanced Fields
body:
Let’s say you’re creating a form to collect information about project completion. You might want to include a “Project Satisfaction Rating” that only appears if the “Project Completed” field is marked as “Yes.” Here’s how you’d set it up:
Add a Boolean field titled “Project Completed” with Yes/No options.
Add a Rating field titled “Project Satisfaction Rating.”
In the Rating field’s settings, under Visible If, set the condition to show this field only if the “Project Completed” field is marked as “Yes.”
This ensures that users will only see and complete the satisfaction rating if the project has been marked as complete, making your form both smarter and more user-friendly.

body:

- Approve the Change Order and generate the AIA invoice again.
- Move the Change Order back to Draft and re-run the AIA to test visibility.If the issue persists or you notice unexpected results, contact the Support Team for assistance.

Even if you are not at the Main Dashboard, you can create a To-Do’s list from almost every screen in Contractor Foreman and there are 2 ways to achieve this.
Option 1: To create a To-Do’s list, go to the Menu and then click on the “plus icon” on the right side to the To-Do’s module and it directly creates a new To-Do’s list right from the dashboard. This will create the “To-Do’s list” for you and will take you to its module.
*** The plus icon only appears when you hover your cursor over the top of the To-Do’s Module.

Option 2: Another way to create a To-Do’s list is by clicking on the “plus calendar icon” located at the bottom right side of the screen, between the calendar and bell icons. Click on it and a new pop up window will appear on the right side of the screen. Make sure the To-Do is selected and then just type the Task Name, which is a required field, and click on the blue button “Save”. Note that this function will not take you to the “To-Do’s” module like the option 1 shown on this article.

These options avoid the extra step of going to the To-Do’s module first and then creating a To-Do’s list from there.

heading: Why It’s Important
body:
Accurate OSHA reports help you:

- Maintain legal compliance with OSHA’s injury and illness recordkeeping requirements (29 CFR 1904).
- Track workplace safety trends to identify and correct recurring hazards.
- Provide evidence of due diligence in case of insurance or inspection reviews.
- Promote a culture of accountability and safety awareness within your organization.

heading: How to Create an OSHA Report in Contractor Foreman
body:
- Go to the Incident Module Navigate to the Incident module from your main dashboard.

- Select or Create the Incident Record

If the event has already been logged, open that Incident Record . If not, click the “+ Incident” button to create a new one and enter all required information such as the type, location, date, time , and description .

- Click on the OSHA 300 Log Button Inside the incident record, locate and click the “OSHA 300 Log” button. This will open a new pop-up window where you can create the OSHA entry.

- Enter the Required Employee and Event Details Fill out the following fields:

Employee name
Event title or brief description of the incident
Location (project or site where it occurred)
Classification (e.g., days away from work, job transfer, or other recordable case)
Injury or illness type (e.g., cut, sprain, burn, respiratory issue, etc.)
- Save the Report Click Save once all required fields are complete. The employee and event will now be recorded in the company’s OSHA 300 Log .

body:
How to Create an Item Group and Use It from the Cost Items Database
Purpose
Item Groups allow you to bundle multiple related Cost Items (materials, labor, etc.) into one reusable group. This makes adding complex assemblies or common task packages to Estimates, Invoices, or Change Orders significantly faster and more consistent. Navigation Steps

- Open the Main Menu

- Click Cost Items Database

- In the top navigation bar of the Cost Items screen, select the Item Groups tab

Steps to Create an Item Group

- In the Item Groups tab, click the dropdown in the top-right corner
- Select “Add Group Item”
- In the popup window:

Enter a Group Name (e.g., “Electrical Outlet”)
Set the Status to Active
Optionally add an Internal Note for team context
- Click the Add/Manage Items button

This opens the item selector where you can choose individual materials, labor, equipment, etc. to include in the group
Specify the default quantities for each line item
- After adding your items, click Save to finalize the Item Group
Using an Item Group
Once an Item Group is created:

- You can use it in modules like Estimates , Invoices , Change Orders , etc.
- Select the Item Group instead of adding each individual line item manually
- After inserting, you can still adjust quantities or pricing as needed
Example: Electrical Contractor
Suppose you’re installing an Electrical Outlet.

Deleting a form in Contractor Foreman is a straightforward process, but it comes with certain limitations depending on the type of form you’re working with. Follow the steps below to delete a form, and be aware of the rules for deleting or archiving specific forms.

Limitations on Deleting Forms:
Used Form: You can delete forms that you have submitted or saved as a draft to submit later under Used Form.
Company Form (Company): You cannot delete custom company forms which are custom created by scratch or by editing a form in the library. You can only archive copied Company Forms if they are no longer needed. Archiving a form will remove it from active use, but the form will still be stored in your system for future reference or reactivation.
Company Form (All): Forms from the Forms & Checklist Library provided by Contractor Foreman cannot be deleted or archived. These forms are pre-loaded by the system and are available to all users at any time.

body: In Contractor Foreman, it’s important to ensure that all line items in your estimates are properly priced. Occasionally, you might have some line items that have a $0 value, indicating they haven’t been priced yet. These items can be quickly identified using a built-in feature that allows you to filter and display any $0 items within your estimate. To begin, go to the Main Menu and select the Estimates module. This module contains all your estimates, and you can access individual estimates from here. Once inside the Estimates module, find the estimate for which you want to view $0 line items. Click on the estimate’s name to open it. After opening the estimate, you’ll be directed to the estimate’s main page. From here, go to the Items Tab on the left-hand panel. This is where all the sections and line items for the estimate are displayed. At the top of the list of sections and line items, you will see a toggle option labeled “Show $0 Items.” This toggle allows you to switch between only displaying line items that have a $0 value or displaying all items. Once you toggle “Show $0 Items” to Yes, the estimate will automatically filter to display all the line items that have a $0 value.

How to Document Attendee Signatures in a Safety Meeting
Purpose
Capturing attendee signatures is an important part of safety compliance. It shows that participants were present, understood the safety topic discussed, and acknowledged their responsibility on the jobsite. These signatures serve as legal and professional proof of meeting participation and are especially helpful during audits, inspections, or internal reviews. Why You Should Capture Signatures

- Meet OSHA and jobsite compliance requirements
- Provide proof of training or safety orientation
- Reinforce accountability among field staff
- Ensure that workers are aware of hazards discussed
- Keep a digital record instead of using paperwork that could get lost
Steps to Add Attendee Signatures

- Go to the Main Menu
- Select Safety Meetings from the menu options

- In the list view, find the Safety Meeting you want to update

Use search or filters if needed
Click on the meeting title to open it

- Scroll down through the Safety Meeting details until you reach the Signatures section to see who has signed their signature.

How Do I Edit the Templates for Estimates, Invoices, and Other Documents? Overview
Contractor Foreman allows you to customize the templates used for Estimates, Invoices, and other modules so your documents match your branding, formatting preferences, and business requirements. These templates control how your documents appear when they are generated and sent to customers. Where to Find Templates
All document templates are managed from within the Settings area of your account. From the main menu, navigate to Settings and scroll down until you reach the Templates section. This is the central location where all editable document templates are stored. Editing Templates

Selecting a module, such as Estimates or Invoices, will load the corresponding template. From there, you can modify text, layout, and available fields to suit your needs. Any updates you save will apply to newly created documents moving forward, ensuring consistency across your future estimates, invoices, and other records.

Contractor Foreman allows you to generate professional, printable PDFs of your project Bills and easily send them via email to employees or any directory contact. This can be helpful for internal documentation, payment verification, or administrative coordination. Whether the recipient needs to verify the Bill, archive it, or take further action, the process of sending a Bill as a PDF is simple and efficient. Follow the steps below to generate and email the PDF version of a Bill directly from the system. Open the Relevant Bill
Start by navigating to the Bills module from the main menu. Locate and click on the specific Bill you want to email. This will open the full details of the Bill. Access the PDF and Email Options
Once you’re inside the Bill, look to the top-right corner of the screen. You’ll see an icon with three vertical dots – this is the actions menu. Click on this icon and then select “View/Email PDF” from the drop-down menu. Choose a PDF Template
After selecting “View/Email PDF,” a new File Preview window will appear. At the top of this window, you’ll find a Templates dropdown menu. Use this to select the desired PDF template you want to apply for formatting the document.

To export the estimate items to a CSV file, first, go to the Main Menu and navigate to the Estimates Module, where you will find all the estimates you’ve created. In the Estimates module, find the specific estimate whose items you want to export into a CSV file. There are two methods to export the items from here:
Method 1: Export from Estimate List
In the list of estimates, locate the estimate you wish to export. Click the three dots to the right of the estimate.

From the drop-down options, select “Export Items to CSV.” This will automatically generate and download a CSV file containing the estimate items.
Method 2: Export from Inside the Estimate
Click on the estimate’s name to open it. Once inside the estimate, click the three dots at the top-right corner of the estimate.

From the drop-down menu, select “Export Items to CSV.” This will generate and download the CSV file for that estimate.
After following either method, a CSV file containing the estimate’s line items will be generated and downloaded to your device. You can open this CSV file using spreadsheet software such as Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, or any other CSV-compatible application.

title: How do I generate a Bill from the Subcontracts Module?

body:
Step 2: Generate a Bill from the Sub-Contract
Once inside the relevant Sub-Contract, follow these steps:

- Click on the three-dot menu (⋮) in the top right corner.
- Select Generate Bill from the drop-down menu. This will open a new Bill entry linked to the Sub-Contract. Select Line Items for Partial Completion
The Bill form will display a list of items from the Sub-Contract.

- Review the list of subcontracted work items.
- For each item, enter the percentage or amount corresponding to the work completed.Example:
If the subcontract includes plumbing work valued at $20,000.00, and the subcontractor has completed 20% of the work, you would:

- Select the plumbing work line item
- Enter 20% completion or $4,000.00 as the amount being billed
- This ensures that only the portion of work completed is reflected in project financials.Create the Bill
After entering all necessary details, click Create Bill to create the Bill. Once the bill is created, you can click the 3 dots to the top right of the bill and post payments to the bill to record payments you’ve made to the sub-contractor.

body: In Contractor Foreman, you have two ways to generate an invoice for a Work Order. Both are valid—it just depends on how you manage your projects and billing. Let’s break them down.
text:
Work Orders > How do I generate an Invoice from a Work Order?

In Contractor Foreman, you have two ways to generate an invoice for a Work Order. Both are valid—it just depends on how you manage your projects and billing. Let’s break them down.
title: How do I generate an Invoice from a Work Order?

heading: Option 1: Create an Invoice Directly from the Work Order
body:
- Open the Work Order .
- Click on the three-dot icon (Action Items).
- Select Create/Modify Invoice .
This creates an invoice tied directly to the Work Order. It’s quick and useful if the Work Order is a side job or extra task that isn’t formally part of the project’s budget or Schedule of Values (SOV).
Important: Invoices created this way will not be reflected in your Schedule of Values. That means you won’t see them in your project’s overall progress billing or partial invoicing reports.
text:
Work Orders > How do I generate an Invoice from a Work Order? :: Option 1: Create an Invoice Directly from the Work Order

- Open the Work Order .
- Click on the three-dot icon (Action Items).
- Select Create/Modify Invoice .
This creates an invoice tied directly to the Work Order. It’s quick and useful if the Work Order is a side job or extra task that isn’t formally part of the project’s budget or Schedule of Values (SOV).
Important: Invoices created this way will not be reflected in your Schedule of Values. That means you won’t see them in your project’s overall progress billing or partial invoicing reports.
title: How do I generate an Invoice from a Work Order?

heading: Option 2: Invoice Through the Schedule of Values
body:
If your Work Order was marked as a Cost Work Order and approved, it automatically adds value to your project’s Schedule of Values. In this case, the better practice is to generate invoices directly through the SOV.
This method ensures:

- Cleaner records of what has (and hasn’t) been invoiced.
- Easier tracking of partial invoicing and progress billing.
- Consistency when managing Change Orders , Work Orders , and your main project contract.

- Easier tracking of partial invoicing and progress billing.
- Consistency when managing Change Orders , Work Orders , and your main project contract.
title: How do I generate an Invoice from a Work Order?

heading: Which method should you use?
body:
- Use the Work Order directly if the task is a “side deal” or extra work not tied to the project’s main contract.
- Use the Schedule of Values if the Work Order is part of the official project scope and you want all invoicing properly tracked within project financials.

title: How do I generate an Invoice from a Work Order?

heading: Real-World Scenario
body:
Imagine your project is almost complete, and the customer asks for a small addition—like painting an extra room. Since the project is basically finished and you don’t need this task added to the SOV, you can simply invoice directly from the Work Order as a separate item.
On the other hand, if the Work Order is created early in the project—for example, building a patio while the main house remodel is still ongoing—you’ll want to keep track of progress and partial billing. In that case, it makes more sense to invoice through the Schedule of Values so everything stays aligned with the project’s financials.

On the right side of the line item you want to modify, click the eyeball icon. This will open that particular item for further editing.

Creating a schedule directly from your Estimate in Contractor Foreman reduces manual data entry and ensures that all costed work items are accounted for in your project schedule.
When you manually change the Estimate Status to Approved, the system will display a pop-up window with several options.

Select the option “Create Schedule from Estimate?” and click Confirm to proceed. Contractor Foreman will automatically generate schedule tasks based on the line items in your estimate, allowing for a smoother transition from planning to execution.
However, this feature is not Available for Online-Approved Estimates. If a customer approves the estimate online, the “Create Schedule from Estimate” option will not be triggered.
You can manually change the Estimate Status back to Estimating and then re-approve it to get the pop-up box again. However, it is not recommended to repeatedly change the estimate status after approval, as it may affect reporting and workflow accuracy.
By utilising this feature, you can enhance project planning efficiency and ensure that all estimated work is properly scheduled.

This feature is particularly useful when dealing with large estimates that need to be pre-populated with specific items, quantities, and costs. To ensure that your CSV file is structured correctly, it’s recommended to use the Contractor Foreman CSV template. This template helps to avoid formatting issues and ensures that the system can accurately identify and import the items. Estimate Import Template
First, navigate to the Estimates Module in the Contractor Foreman system. Once you’re in the Estimates Module, locate and select the Estimate you want to import items into. Click on the estimate name to open it. In the estimate, go to the Items tab from the left panel. This is where you can view and manage all of your estimate’s line items. Just below the Estimate Financial Summary, you will find the Add Item to Estimate drop-down menu to the right. Click on it, and from the available options, select Import Items from CSV File. A pop-up window will appear, allowing you to upload your CSV file.

Review the preview carefully to make sure everything is properly aligned and that no important data is missing.

body: In Contractor Foreman, the ability to import expenses into a Bill streamlines the process of consolidating project costs. This feature allows you to pull in previously recorded expenses directly into a Bill, making sure your financial records stay accurate and organized without requiring you to manually re-enter data. Start by navigating to the Bills module from the main menu. Create a new Bill or Locate and click on the Bill to which you want to add the expense. This will open the Bill’s details. Once in side of the Bill, whether you created it or opened an existing one look for the “Add Item to Bill” dropdown menu and from there, select “Import from Expenses”. This menu can be accessed by clicking the 3-dot icon in the Lump Sum/Item Costs table. This will open a window showing the list of recorded expenses that are eligible for import. These are typically expenses that have been logged under the same project but are not yet associated with any Bill. Choose the Expense(s) to Import, from the list, review and select the expense(s) that you want to bring into the Bill. You can select one or multiple items depending on your needs. After selecting the expenses, click Save & Close.

title: How do I import Expenses into a Bill?

body:
Choose the Expense(s) to Import, from the list, review and select the expense(s) that you want to bring into the Bill. You can select one or multiple items depending on your needs. After selecting the expenses, click Save & Close. The imported expenses will now appear as line items in the Bill, ready for review, adjustment, or further processing. Once imported:

- The expense(s) become part of the Bill and are tracked as part of that Bill’s total.
- The original expense entries remain in the system, but now have a clear association with the Bill.
- This helps maintain traceability between incidental purchases and formal billing documents. Importing expenses into a Bill in Contractor Foreman is a practical feature for keeping your job costing and vendor payments accurate. It saves time, ensures consistency, and reduces administrative workload by leveraging previously recorded information.

body:
In residential or commercial construction, subcontractors and vendors often complete portions of their agreed-upon work or deliveries at various stages throughout the project. Once part of the work is completed or a portion of materials is delivered, they will typically submit an invoice requesting payment for the corresponding value. In Contractor Foreman, this type of invoice is recorded as a Bill.
This article explains how you can generate a Bill from an existing Sub-Contract or Purchase Order, and how to record partial or full payments while keeping your project’s financials up to date.

title: How do I generate a Bill from a Purchase Order or Subcontract?

heading: When Should You Generate a Bill?
body:
A Bill should be generated when:

- A subcontractor completes part of their scope of work and submits an invoice.
- A vendor fulfills part or in its full of a Purchase Order and requests payment.
- You want to track actual costs against committed budgets.
- You need to manage progress payments and retention on subcontracted work.
