heading: Generating a Bill from a Sub-Contract
body:
Access the Sub-Contracts Module
From the Main Menu, select Sub-Contracts. Locate and open the Sub-Contract you want to create a Bill for. Generate the Bill
Once inside the Sub-Contract, click the three-dot menu (⋮) in the top-right corner of the screen. Select Generate Bill from the drop-down list. This action will open a new Bill entry screen that is automatically linked to the Sub-Contract. Enter Completion Details
The Bill form will show a list of line items from the Sub-Contract. For each item, review the line items and enter the percentage that reflects the portion of work completed to date. Example:
If the subcontract includes Electrical work valued at $15,000, and the subcontractor has completed 10%, you would: Enter 10% or $1,500.00 as the billed amount. This ensures that only the portion of the work completed is reflected in the financial records, with the remaining value still available for future billing. Create the Bill
Once you’ve entered all necessary details, click Generate Bill to finalize the entry. After the Bill is created, It will appear under the Bills module and also within the Documents tab of the associated Sub-Contract.

To import cost codes into Contractor Foreman by Excel, please go to the Menu and choose Settings. From here choose Cost Codes.
You will see an Action drop down on the top left. Click it and then choose Import Cost Codes (From File). The template header that exists within the Template should also exists within your uploaded document. We do not require your codes to have a Parent or Child #, but the column must exists (even if blank values are within it).
If the value already exists, it will be ignored and a duplicate will not be created.
In the event that an import was later found to have errors or needed to be deleted, you can click on the Action menu within the Cost Codes page and click on Previous Imports. You will then see a list of imports that can be deleted to undo the recent import.

Contractor Foreman makes it easy to save time and avoid double entry by importing items directly from an Estimate into a Work Order.
Here’s how to do it:

- Open the Work Order you want to edit.
- Scroll down to the Details section.
- Click on Add Item to Work Order .
- From the drop-down menu, select Import from Estimate .
- A pop-up window will appear on the right side of your screen.
- Browse through the Estimate and pick the item(s) you want to include in this Work Order.
- Click Save & Close, and you’re done.

By importing from the Estimate, you’re keeping your records consistent and eliminating the need to re-type line items. This not only saves time but also reduces errors, since everything flows from the original Estimate you already built for the project.
text:
Work Orders > How do I import specific estimate items into a Work Order?

Contractor Foreman makes it easy to save time and avoid double entry by importing items directly from an Estimate into a Work Order.
Here’s how to do it:

- Open the Work Order you want to edit.
- Scroll down to the Details section.
- Click on Add Item to Work Order .
- From the drop-down menu, select Import from Estimate .
- A pop-up window will appear on the right side of your screen.
- Browse through the Estimate and pick the item(s) you want to include in this Work Order.
- Click Save & Close, and you’re done.

By importing from the Estimate, you’re keeping your records consistent and eliminating the need to re-type line items. This not only saves time but also reduces errors, since everything flows from the original Estimate you already built for the project.
title: How do I import specific estimate items into a Work Order?

body: In Contractor Foreman, you can generate invoices directly from your Service Tickets, helping keep all your billing organized and consistent with your workflow.
text:
Service Tickets > How do I invoice the Customer for Service Tickets?

In Contractor Foreman, you can generate invoices directly from your Service Tickets, helping keep all your billing organized and consistent with your workflow.
title: How do I invoice the Customer for Service Tickets?

heading: Step 1: Complete the Service Ticket (Recommended)
body:
While it’s technically possible to create an invoice at any time, we recommend changing the Service Ticket status to “Completed” before invoicing.
This keeps your workflow clean and ensures that all work details have been finalized before charging the customer.
💡 Tip: If you prefer to invoice ahead of time, you can. The ability to create an invoice is not tied to the status of the Service Ticket — but consistency is key for tracking and reporting.

Contractor Foreman makes it easy to track which files are shared with your client and provides tools to control access to those files. Navigate to the project for which you want to check shared files. Once inside the project, click on the Client Access tab. Scroll down to the section “Shared Files & Photos”. Here, you’ll see a grid view of the files shared with the client. Notably, files shared with clients can also be attached to submissions through other modules. For instance, if you submit an estimate or invoice that includes attached files, those files may still be visible to the client in the submitted estimate PDF file), you just need to keep in mind the following:
For each file listed, Contractor Foreman provides a simple visual indicator to show whether the file has been shared with the client. In the top right corner of each file’s thumbnail, you’ll see a person-shaped icon. This icon becomes visible when you hover your mouse over a file. If the person icon is highlighted, the file has been shared with your client. If the person icon is not highlighted, the file is hidden from the client. If the person icon is highlighted and you want to stop sharing the file, click on the icon.

Contractor Foreman offers a flexible way to control what projects your employees can view. Before you can limit access, the employee must have their own user account within Contractor Foreman. (Click here to learn How do I setup a new User and send email with Login credentials?)
From the main menu, click on Directory and locate the employee you want to give login access to. Open the employee’s profile. On the left-hand panel of their profile, click on the Details tab. Find the section called Access Details. In the Access Details section, you’ll find the field labeled Viewable Projects, which controls which projects the employee can access. By default, this field is set to All, meaning the employee has access to all the projects within Contractor Foreman. To limit access, switch the setting from All to Some. Once you select Some, you will be prompted to choose which specific projects the employee can view. You can now manually select the projects that you want the employee to have access to. In Contractor Foreman, project access works on a permissive model. This means you can allow access to specific projects rather than outright restrict access to certain ones.

body: To link a contractor to a bid package in Contractor Foreman, follow these steps. Start by navigating to the Bid Manager module from the Main Menu. Here, you will find a list of the bid packages you’ve created so far. Each package corresponds to a specific estimate that you are looking to receive bids on. Identify the bid package to which you want to add a contractor. To add a subcontractor in the Bid Manager dashboard, first identify the bid package to which you want to add the subcontractor. On the right-hand side of the screen, click the Open in a New Tab icon — this will open the Bid Manager section within the Estimate. Once there, open and edit the bid package where you want to add the subcontractor. From that window, you’ll be able to include the subcontractor and make any necessary adjustments to the bid package. In the Edit Mode of the bid package, navigate to the Bidders Tab. This is where you will manage all the contractors and bidders associated with this specific package. To add a new contractor to the bid package, click on the Add Bidder button. This will prompt a list of your contractors. From this list, select the contractor you wish to link to the bid package.

In Contractor Foreman, making a Change Order reflect a negative value is straightforward and can be done by adjusting the quantity of the item in question. If a reduction in costs or materials is required, simply input a negative quantity in the “QTY” field when adding or editing an item within the Change Order.
For example, if an original Change Order reduced the quantity of an item by 10 units, you can enter “-10” in the QTY field. The system will automatically calculate the negative value based on the unit cost and other associated details, such as tax and markup, if applicable. This will result in a negative total for that line item, effectively reducing theoverall Change Order value.

Overview
The Cover Sheet feature allows you to customize the introductory section of your Estimate. This is often the first thing a client sees, so it’s a great place to personalize your presentation with client details, company information, and a professional message. Accessing the Cover Sheet

- Go to the Menu .
- Select Estimates .

- Choose the Estimate you want to modify.

- On the left-hand menu, select Cover Sheet . Using the Cover Sheet Options
Inside the Cover Sheet editor, you’ll see placeholder fields surrounded by brackets (e.g., [PROJECT_NAME], [CUSTOMER_FIRST], [USER_COMPANY]). These placeholders automatically pull data from your Estimate, Customer, and Company settings.

In many construction projects, costs incurred from vendors or subcontractors may need to be passed on to the client, often with a markup to account for overhead or profit. Contractor Foreman makes this easy by allowing you to generate an Invoice directly from a Bill and apply markup to individual line items before sending it to your customer. This article will guide you through the process of creating an invoice from a Bill, marking up the relevant items, and submitting it to your customer. Open the Bill
From the Main Menu, go to the Bills module. Find and open the Bill that you would like to invoice to your customer. This Bill should reflect the costs you have incurred and now wish to pass on to the client. Generate an Invoice from the Bill
Inside the Bill, look to the top-right corner of the screen. Click the three-dot icon (⋮) to open the actions menu. Select Generate Invoice from the drop-down. This will automatically create a new Invoice that includes the same line items as the Bill, linking both documents together for tracking purposes. Apply Markup to Line Items
In the newly created Invoice, go to the Items tab. You will see a list of all the items that were pulled from the Bill.

Whether you’re ordering materials, scheduling services, or allocating labor costs, the Items section allows you to build a precise breakdown of what’s being purchased, complete with cost tracking, quantities, discounts, and more. Contractor Foreman provides multiple flexible methods to populate a PO based on where your information originates: from preloaded item libraries, estimates, project billing structures, or through manual entry. Navigation Steps

1. Access the Purchase Order Module

- Click on the Main Menu ( ☰ ) .

- Scroll down and select “Purchase Orders.”
You will be directed to the Purchase Order dashboard, where all POs are listed and sortable by:

- Project Name
- Vendor
- PO Status (Draft, Submitted, Approved, etc.)
- Date
- PO Number
2. Locate and Open the Specific Purchase Order

- Use the filters (e.g., Project Name, Vendor, Status) to locate the PO you want to add items to.
- Click on the PO entry to open its Details View . 3.

heading: Posting Payments to Invoices in Contractor Foreman
body:
Accurate payment tracking is essential to maintaining healthy financial records and ensuring strong client relationships. In Contractor Foreman, posting a payment directly to an invoice provides a reliable way to confirm what has been received, monitor outstanding balances, and create a clear audit trail for both your team and your clients.
By entering payments into the system, you reduce the risk of miscommunication, improve cash flow visibility, and strengthen your company’s financial accountability. Contractor Foreman allows you to log all the necessary details—from payment type to verification status—so every invoice reflects the most accurate information.

heading: Why Posting Payments Matters
body:
Invoices are the financial backbone of any project. Without a structured system to record payments, businesses risk:

- Overlooking received funds due to manual tracking errors.
- Delays in reconciliation between invoicing and accounting systems.
- Confusion with clients regarding balances, partial payments, or failed transactions.
- Loss of transparency in project reporting.Contractor Foreman eliminates these risks by giving you a simple but comprehensive way to attach payments directly to invoices. Each entry becomes part of the permanent record, ensuring all stakeholders can trust the numbers.

heading: How to Post a Payment to an Invoice
body:
Follow these steps to correctly post a payment to an existing invoice in Contractor Foreman:

- Open the Invoice Module

From the main menu, select Invoices .

Browse or search for the specific invoice to which you want to apply a payment.
- Access the Payment Tab

Once inside the invoice, select Payments from the left-hand menu.

This section is dedicated to tracking all payments tied to the selected invoice.
- Post a New Payment

Click the three-dot action icon in the Payments tab.

Select Post Payment to Invoice .
- Enter Payment Details Complete the payment form with the following fields:

Date: The date the payment was received.

Amount: The amount received for this payment.

Payment Type: Choose from Bank Transfer, Cash, Credit, Check, or Other.

Status: Mark the payment as Received, In Review, Verified, or Failed.

Payment Notes: Add any relevant comments or clarifications.

Reference #: Enter transaction IDs, check numbers, or other reference identifiers.
- Save the Payment

Once all fields are completed, click Save to apply the payment.

The payment will now be listed under the invoice’s Payment tab, updating the balance due accordingly.

heading: Best Practices for Payment Tracking
body:
To make the most of this feature, keep the following practices in mind:

- Verify statuses promptly: Use the “In Review” or “Verified” options to ensure that only cleared payments are treated as final.
- Use payment notes consistently: Notes help internal teams quickly identify unusual cases, such as partial payments or client-specific arrangements.
- Reference all transactions: Always record a check number, bank confirmation, or transaction ID to maintain a verifiable audit trail.
- Monitor failed payments: Payments marked as “Failed” should be followed up immediately to avoid project delays.

heading: How to Properly Post a Payment for a Service Ticket
body:
Since direct payments to Service Tickets are not possible, the correct workflow is as follows:

- Create an Invoice from the Service Ticket

Open the Service Ticket.

Use the “Create Invoice” option to generate an invoice for the services provided.
- Post the Payment Against the Invoice

Once the customer’s payment has been received and confirmed, post it against the invoice that was generated for the Service Ticket.

This ensures the payment is properly tracked in both your financial records and reporting.

body:
To post a payment to an invoice in Contractor Foreman, navigate to the Invoices Module from the main menu. From the list of invoices displayed, select the specific invoice to which you want to post a payment.
Once inside the invoice, click the three dots in the top right corner and select “Post Payment to Invoice.” You will be prompted to enter the following details:

Payment Date*: The date the payment was made.
Amount*: The amount being paid.
Payment Type*: Select the method of payment (e.g., bank transfer, check, cash).
Approval Status*: Choose whether the payment is approved or pending.
Payment Notes: Any additional information about the payment.
Reference #: Enter the reference number, such as a cheque or transaction number, if applicable.

After entering the required details, click “Apply” to post the payment.
Once the payment is recorded, you can view it under the “Payments” tab within the invoice.

If there is still a balance due, it will be reflected in both the “Items” tab and the “Payments” tab. Unless the invoice is fully paid, it will not be marked as paid. Once the invoice is fully paid, it will automatically be marked as paid.

heading: Why is printing a punch list important?
body:
Even though Contractor Foreman allows your team to access and update punch lists directly from the mobile app, there are scenarios where having a printed copy makes a big difference:

- Limited internet or no device access – Not all field teams have smartphones, tablets, or reliable internet on-site. A printed punch list ensures they still know exactly what needs to be done.
- Hands-on crews – Some laborers or subcontractors prefer to work with a piece of paper they can carry, mark up, and refer to quickly without worrying about devices.
- Clear jobsite communication – By handing off a printed punch list, you can be confident everyone on-site has the same list of tasks and corrections to complete.
- Backtracking and documentation – Keeping a printed record of punch lists is helpful for compliance, quality control, and as proof of what work was requested and completed.
Printing is not about replacing the digital workflow—it’s about adding flexibility. Contractor Foreman gives you the power to choose what works best for your team: fully digital tracking in the app or traditional printed copies when the situation requires it.

Managing projects in Contractor Foreman often involves keeping track of completed projects while ensuring that the workspace remains clutter-free. You may want to remove completed projects from active lists but still retain their details for future reference. From the main navigation menu in Contractor Foreman, click on the Projects module. Once you are inside the projects module, you will see a list of all the projects currently in your account. By default, this list only showsopen projects. If you’re looking for completed projects, or all open and completed projects, just above the list of projects, you will see a filtering option on the right-hand side. The filter options include:
Open: Displays only ongoing projects. Completed: Displays projects marked as completed. All: Displays all projects, regardless of their status. To locate the project you wish to hide, select Completed to view projects that are finished. Once you locate the completed project from the list, you can archive it so that it is removed from the active project list but still retrievable for historical reference.

body: The Access Code is a useful feature within Contractor Foreman, particularly for tracking property access details, such as entry codes or gate codes. This information ensures that field personnel, such as the Foreman, can easily enter a property when required, without delays or complications. The Access/Gate Code is stored within the Customer record in the Directory. It can hold any access codes or security gate information necessary for entering a property or job site. If you want to restrict who can see or access the Gate/Access Code, this can be controlled through user roles. To manage roles, first, go to the Main Menu and select Settings. Inside Settings, select the Roles section. This is where you can manage the permissions assigned to different users or user groups within your organization. Once inside the Roles section, click the green pencil icon of the role you wish to modify, scroll down to the section labelled Directory. Within the Directory permissions, locate the option for Customer Access Code (Field) and adjust the permission setting for specific roles.

body: Internal Notes play a vital role in documenting key information and communication within a project. However, there may be times when you want to keep certain notes private and restrict them from being viewed by other users in Contractor Foreman. Here’s how you can manage this by ensuring that notes remain private. From the main Menu, go to the Projects module and select the project where the note is associated. Once you’ve opened the project, click on the Documents tab located in the left panel. Within the Documents tab, scroll down until you find the Notes section. This will display a list of all notes that have been created for the selected project. Find the note you want to restrict. You can either click the preview icon or the open-in-new-window icon to view it in full detail. Once the note is opened, look for the green pencil icon in the upper-right corner. Click this icon to enter the edit mode for the note. Just below the tags section, you will find a checkbox labeled Make Private: Visible Only to Me. Check this box to restrict the note from being viewed by anyone else in the system. After you’ve marked the note as private, click Save to ensure that the restriction is applied.

body: In Contractor Foreman, managing access to specific projects for employees or contractors can be done once you allow login access to them. By default, employees and contractors can view all projects, but you can modify their access to only certain projects when needed. First, navigate to the Directory module from the main menu. Here, you’ll find all your contacts, including employees and contractors. Scroll through the contact list or use filters to find the employee or contractor whose project access you want to manage. Click on their name to go to their profile. In the employee’s or contractor’s profile, look for the widget called Access Details. Within this widget, you’ll find an option labelled Viewable Projects. By default, the Viewable Projects setting is set to “All,” meaning the employee or contractor can access all active projects. To restrict this, change the setting from All to Some. A list of projects will appear, allowing you to select the specific projects you want the employee or contractor to have access to. After selecting the relevant projects, click Save to confirm the changes.

body: In Contractor Foreman, restricting the ability to delete records is managed through role settings. By configuring which roles have the access to delete records, you can prevent users from accidentally or intentionally deleting important records, such as estimates, projects, or financial data. Begin by going to the Menu and navigating to the Settings module. From there, choose the Roles section. Here, you will see a list of all existing roles in your system. Choose the role you want to modify by clicking on the green pencil icon next to it, which will bring you to the Edit screen. If you want to create a new role, you can click on Add Role and proceed to define the permissions for this new role. You will see a checkbox labelled “Allow this Role to Delete Items” just below the Notes field within the role. This checkbox controls whether users assigned to this role can delete records in Contractor Foreman or not. If the box is checked, users with this role will have the permission to delete records, such as estimates, projects, or financial data. If the box is unchecked, users assigned to this role will not be able to delete any items.

body: If you have multiple projects running simultaneously, you may want to control which ones appear on your scheduling dashboard. This can help reduce clutter and improve performance, especially if some projects are large or resource-intensive. Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to select which projects are displayed on your schedule. From the main Menu, click on the Schedule module. This will open the scheduling dashboard where your Gantt charts and task lists are managed. On the upper left-hand side of the Schedule module, you will see a button labeled Projects. Click this button to bring up a list of all the projects in your Contractor Foreman account. From the list that appears, you can select which projects you want to show on the Gantt chart. You can toggle the projects on or off by checking or unchecking them. This allows you to filter which projects appear on your schedule. It’s important to note that selecting too many projects, particularly large or complex ones, can slow down the performance of the Schedule module. This issue is typically related to the capacity of your graphics card.

heading: Overview
body:
In Contractor Foreman, you can control what level of detail your client sees when you send a proposal. Some clients prefer to view only the final total amount, while others may want to see a full breakdown of all line items.
If you want to send a proposal that displays only the total amount—without showing individual material, labor, or itemized details—you can do so by selecting the Lump Sum Total Only template before sending or viewing your Estimate as a PDF.
This article explains how to use that feature, along with important notes and best practices.

body:

From the main Menu , select Estimates under the Financial section.

This will open the list of all Estimates created in your account.

Use the search bar or filters to find the Estimate you want to send as a proposal.

Click the Estimate to open its details page.
- Access the PDF View Options

Once inside the Estimate, click the 3-dot icon on the right and select View/Email PDF .
- Choose the “Lump Sum Total Only” Template

This template displays just the final total amount , omitting all line-item details from the Estimate.
- Review and Send the Proposal

Review the generated PDF to confirm it shows only the total amount and all relevant company and client information.

Click Send to email the proposal directly to your client, or download the PDF for manual sharing.

A consistent numbering structure prevents confusion, ensures chronological accuracy, and makes it easier to reference documents later. Contractor Foreman allows each module to follow a numbering format that best reflects your business practices.

title: How do I set the initial Numbering for each of the Features?

body:
A consistent numbering structure prevents confusion, ensures chronological accuracy, and makes it easier to reference documents later. Contractor Foreman allows each module to follow a numbering format that best reflects your business practices. To configure numbering for each feature:

- Navigate to Settings from the main menu and select Custom .
- Scroll to Customized Starting Number and click the green pencil icon to edit.
- For each module (e.g., Estimate, Invoice, Work Order, Change Order, Purchase Order), select one of the following:

Start at Number : Define a starting point (e.g., begin Invoices at 1001). Custom Text : Assign identifiers manually when creating items. Auto/Custom : Allow the system to automatically generate identifiers.

heading: Numbering Options Explained
body:
Each module in Contractor Foreman—such as Estimates, Invoices, Work Orders, Change Orders, and RFIs-can be configured to follow a numbering method that fits the way your organization operates. This ensures that every document is tracked in a consistent and meaningful way. When editing the numbering settings for a module, you’ll see the following options:

- Start at Number

This option allows you to set a fixed number where the sequence begins. For example, if you want invoices to begin at 1001 rather than 1 , you can enter that starting point. Each new invoice will then follow sequentially (1002, 1003, and so on). This is ideal for companies that already use a numbering system and want Contractor Foreman to continue the sequence without interruption. Custom Text (Applied Manually per Item)

With this option, numbering is not automatic. Instead, users manually assign identifiers each time a new record is created. This gives you full control and flexibility—for example, you may want to use unique project codes, client references, or other custom identifiers that don’t follow a strict numeric sequence.

In Contractor Foreman, you can attach files—such as images, blueprints, or supporting documents—to your Estimates. By default, these files remain internal and are not visible to clients. However, if you want to share these attachments with a Customer or Lead, you can easily enable them to appear in the Estimate PDF.

A credit in an expense refers to a negative entry that offsets or reduces the total cost of a project or account. This typically happens when there’s a refund, rebate, or an adjustment to a previously logged expense.
For example, if you return a purchased item like extra paint or unused materials, the refunded amount is entered as a credit (negative number) in the expense record. This ensures that the total project costs are accurate and reflect the actual money spent.
Using credits properly helps maintain precise financial records and ensures accountability in project budgets, especially in residential construction where small adjustments can impact overall costs.
To show an Expense in negative amount, enter the Expense and place a – (negative sign) in front of the amount.

Tracking all the payments made by your company for a specific project is crucial to ensure financial transparency and proper accounting of expenses. Contractor Foreman allows you to easily track payments made to vendors, subcontractors, and other expenses related to a project. Additionally, you can monitor labor costs from employee timecards.
To get an overview of the total actual costs spent on the project, go to the Projects module from the main menu and select the relevant project. Once inside the project, go to the Summary tab. In the Work in Progress (WIP) section, you’ll see a summary of the total actual costs for the project.

This includes payments made to vendors and subcontractors, expenses recorded, and time card costs for employees and contractors. This gives a high-level overview of where your money is going for the project.

heading: Detailed Payment Tracking
body:
To track specific payments made by your company to vendors or subcontractors for a project, go to the Financials tab from the left panel. Inside the Financials tab, you will see a section that lists all the bills. For each Bill record, you can see:
Total Bill: The total amount owed for that specific bill. Balance Due: How much is still unpaid, if any. The total amount shown on top represents what you have been already charged by Vendor or Subcontractors, in other words the summary of all your Bills. This section is particularly useful for tracking payments made to vendors and subcontractors. It keeps a running record of all the payments associated with each bill in the project. Scroll down below the Bills section, and you’ll find a list of all Expenses recorded for the project. Expenses might include several related project expenses that have been paid by your company. To track labor costs for the project, on the left panel of the project, navigate to the Time tab. Here, you’ll see a summary of the total hours worked on the project, along with the total cost associated with those time records.

body: To calculate and track retention for invoices, first, you need to set up the retention rate for the project. Navigate to the project from the main menu by selecting the “Projects” module and opening the respective project. Once inside the project, go to the “Details” tab from the left-hand panel. In this tab, find the “Additional Details” area. Click the “View All” icon located in the top right corner to expand the section. In the expanded view, locate the “Retention %” field. Here, enter the retention percentage that applies to your invoices. For instance, if your contract with the client specifies a 10% retainage, you should enter “10” in this field. From this point forward, the system will automatically apply a 10% deduction for retainage on all invoices associated with this project. If you need to change the retention percentage at any point, simply update the value in the “Retention %” field. However, note that any changes will only apply to future invoices and will not affect previously created invoices.

To un-archive or reactivate an invoice in Contractor Foreman, begin by navigating to the Invoices module from the Main Menu. Once in the Invoices module, locate the Invoices Filter option in the top left corner.

Click on the filter, and from the Record Status dropdown, select “Archived” to display all invoices that have been archived. After making this selection, click “Apply” to filter the results.

You will now see a list of archived invoices. To reactivate a specific invoice, you have two options. First, you can click on status under the item name, then select the a new status from the menu that appears.

This process will change the status of the invoice from archived to active, allowing you to continue working on it or apply any necessary updates. By reactivating the invoice, it will be fully functional within the system and available for edits, payments, or any other actions that may be required.

heading: Automatic Notifications and Actions
body:
Some statuses trigger automatic actions or notifications:

- Scheduled → En Route When you switch to En Route , the system will prompt a message asking if you’d like to notify the customer that the technician is on the way.

When a Payment is made toward a Project’s Invoice, it should be recorded in Contractor Foreman to ensure your financial records remain accurate and up to date.
Payments can be added using the Post Payment feature. This allows you to document how and when the customer paid, link the payment to the correct invoice, and update the project’s outstanding balance automatically.
text:

When a Payment is made toward a Project’s Invoice, it should be recorded in Contractor Foreman to ensure your financial records remain accurate and up to date.
Payments can be added using the Post Payment feature. This allows you to document how and when the customer paid, link the payment to the correct invoice, and update the project’s outstanding balance automatically.
title: When to add payment for project?

heading: When You Should Add a Payment
body:
You should add a payment whenever money is received from a client for work completed under a project. Common examples include:

- After sending an invoice and receiving a full or partial payment.
- When a customer pays a deposit or progress payment on a milestone-based project.
- Once a change order has been billed and paid separately.
- When closing out a project and collecting the final balance.By entering the payment right away, you maintain accurate financial reporting, prevent duplicate charges, and ensure your Accounts Receivable records reflect the true outstanding amount.

heading: Where to Add a Payment

- You can attach any supporting files (e.g., payment receipts or bank confirmations) for documentation.

Accurate job costing is crucial for effective financial tracking and budget management in any construction project. In Contractor Foreman, ensuring that a Bill is properly job costed means aligning billable items with your project’s Schedule of Values (SOV) and using consistent Cost Codes across related documents.
This article explains how to ensure that a Bill is accurately job costed—whether it is generated automatically from a Purchase Order (PO) or Sub-Contract, or entered manually.
text:
Bills > How do I make sure a Bill is accurately job costed? :: Overview

Accurate job costing is crucial for effective financial tracking and budget management in any construction project. In Contractor Foreman, ensuring that a Bill is properly job costed means aligning billable items with your project’s Schedule of Values (SOV) and using consistent Cost Codes across related documents.
This article explains how to ensure that a Bill is accurately job costed—whether it is generated automatically from a Purchase Order (PO) or Sub-Contract, or entered manually.
title: How do I make sure a Bill is accurately job costed?

heading: 1. Use Cost Items from the Project’s Schedule of Values (SOV)
body:
The most effective way to ensure consistent job costing is to use the same cost items and cost codes from the project’s Schedule of Values.

- These items are typically assigned during the estimating phase and include Labor , Materials , Subcontractor Work , and Equipment .
- Cost Codes categorize each cost item, allowing you to track expenses under specific divisions or categories in the Job Cost Report .

heading: 2. Generate Bills Directly from Purchase Orders or Sub-Contracts
body:
If your Bill is related to a Purchase Order or Sub-Contract, always try to generate it directly from those sources.

- This creates a seamless link between the estimate, commitment (PO/Sub-Contract), and actual cost (Bill).
- The Cost Items and Cost Codes will flow automatically, maintaining consistency across the project’s financial records.
- This method reduces manual entry errors and ensures the Bill is connected to previously committed costs.

Restricting the cost codes that are displayed when using the Timecard feature in Contractor Foreman is important for reducing complexity and minimizing the risk of employees selecting incorrect codes. There are three main ways to control which cost codes are shown in time cards: by unchecking specific cost codes for time card use or by enabling Project-Based Cost Codes and using Labor only cost codes. Yes — all your Opportunity details remain intact after creating an Estimate. When you create an Estimate from within an Opportunity, the system simply links the Estimate to that Opportunity record. Nothing is removed or altered.
Your Opportunity — including its details, attachments, notes, photos, and any other information — stays exactly as it is.
However, once the Estimate is approved, the Opportunity will automatically convert into a Project. When that happens, all the information from the Opportunity (notes, files, estimate, etc.) will seamlessly transfer over to the new Project record, ensuring that no data is lost in the process.
In short:

- Creating an Estimate does not affect your Opportunity details.
- Approving the Estimate simply converts your Opportunity into a Project — keeping all your data connected and organized.

body: When working in construction, inspections and permits go hand in hand. Every inspection that takes place on your jobsite is almost always tied to a permit, whether it’s structural, plumbing, electrical, or occupancy-related. That’s why Contractor Foreman gives you the option to connect Permit Details directly to an Inspection record.
text:
Inspections > Why to add inspection in Permit Details, what is the purpose to add it?

When working in construction, inspections and permits go hand in hand. Every inspection that takes place on your jobsite is almost always tied to a permit, whether it’s structural, plumbing, electrical, or occupancy-related. That’s why Contractor Foreman gives you the option to connect Permit Details directly to an Inspection record.
title: Why to add inspection in Permit Details, what is the purpose to add it?

heading: What is the purpose?
body:
By adding the permit information to your inspections, you ensure that everything is properly documented and easy to trace.

- Track Inspections against Permits : Each inspection can be tied back to the permit that required it, making compliance clear and well-documented.
- Backtracking made simple : If questions arise later—whether from inspectors, clients, or auditors—you can quickly pull up the inspection history for a specific permit.
- Meet compliance requirements : Many cities, counties, and agencies track inspections by permit numbers . By using the same method, you stay aligned with how inspectors operate.
- Maintain construction standards : Linking permits and inspections ensures that your work is always meeting the required safety and quality benchmarks.

heading: Why does it matter?
body:
Think of permits and inspections as two sides of the same coin. Without tying them together, you risk gaps in your records, making it harder to prove compliance, resolve disputes, or track progress. With them linked, you create a seamless chain of documentation that keeps your projects professional, organized, and inspection-ready at any moment.

Adding Permit Details to Inspections isn’t just about filling out a field, it’s about creating a clear compliance trail that protects your company and keeps your projects on track.

text:

There are two ways to create a Gantt chart for a project, which are: creating a Gantt chart from the approved estimate or creating a Gantt chart manually.
title: How do I create a Gantt chart for any project and track that project?

heading: Creating a Gantt chart from the Approved Estimate
body:
If the Estimate status gets updated to “Approved” manually, you’ll get the option to create a schedule from your Approved Estimate line items. If you choose that option, all of your Estimate line items will be converted into tasks on the Gantt chart of the Project.
https://kb.contractorforeman.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/CREATE-AN-SCHEDULE-FROM-THE-ESTIMATE.mp4
However, if the Estimate was approved online by the customer, a Gantt chart will not be created automatically from the Approved Estimate and you will not get the option to create a schedule from the Approved Estimate. Nevertheless, you can move your Estimate status back to “Estimating”, and move it back to “Approved” to get the option to create a schedule from the Approved Estimate. The below video, will show you an Estimate that has been approved and its Project, which originally does not have a Gantt Chart, then the Estimate status will be changed from “Approved” to “Estimating” and back to “Approved”, in order to have the option to generate the Gantt Chart.
https://kb.contractorforeman.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/RE-APPROVING-AN-ESTIMATE-TO-CREATE-A-SCHEDULE.mp4

heading: Creating a Gantt chart manually for a Project
body:
Once you have a project created, go to the Schedule module and select that Project from the Project list using the “Projects” button on the top left of the Gantt chart.

Once you select your new project and click Save, a popup window will appear asking for a Start Date and an End Date for your project. The date period you enter will be considered as the project duration to create the Gantt chart. Once you enter a date period and proceed, a Gantt chart will be created with a single task with the time period you’ve entered as the project duration. Don’t worry! you can always customize your project’s start date, end date, and duration on the Gantt chart.

heading: Overview
body:
In Contractor Foreman, the Bidding feature allows you to manage and track all bid invitations, responses, and quotes from your Vendors or Subcontractors in one centralized location. Using the Bidding tab within an Estimate, you can send bid invitations, monitor activity, and record or compare submitted pricing.
Important:
Contractor Foreman allows you to send and track bid-related emails but does not receive or store incoming emails. Vendors or Subcontractors must reply to your invitations directly via their own email, and you can manually record or upload their quotes in the Bidding tab.

This system streamlines bid management, provides visibility into who has received or opened your invitations, and helps you make informed decisions when selecting Vendors or Subcontractors.

body: In Contractor Foreman, it is not possible to generate an invoice directly from a Change Order (CO). Instead, the Invoice must be created first, and then the Change Order items can be imported into the invoice. Remember that the Change Order will be automatically added to the Schedule of Values once it has been approved (manually or by the customer). Once you have generated an invoice, go to the “Add Items to Invoice” option. From there, select the “Import from Schedule of Values” option. This will display a list of all line items included in the Schedule of Values, including any recently approved change order items. You will be able to select the specific items you wish to include in the invoice. It is important to note that only change orders with the status of “Approved” and “Unbilled” will appear in this dropdown, ensuring that only the valid and necessary items are included in your invoice. One of the benefits of using the Schedule of Values in Contractor Foreman is that approved change orders are automatically updated into the SOV and you will be able to track invoiced percentages.

This means that when a change order is approved, you don’t need to manually enter these items into the invoice, they will automatically appear in the SOV , ready to be imported when you are generating the invoice. heading: Create a New Note from the Notes Module
body:
From the Main Menu, navigate to the Notes module. Click the + icon located on the left-hand side of the Notes screen to create a new note.

In the Project field, you will see the option to link the note to a specific project. This step is optional, and you can choose to leave this field blank if the note is not related to any project. If you want to link it to a project, select the desired project from the drop-down list.
Title: Give your note a descriptive title.
Status: By default, the status is set to Open. You can change this status as required to Closed.
Priority: Set the priority of the note as Low, Normal, or High depending on its importance.
Add Notes: Input the details or description you want to include in the note. You can also add multiple note records.
Tags: You can assign tags to categorize the note further for easy filtering and searchability.
Attach Files: Attach any relevant files or documents to your note for better documentation.

After filling in all the necessary details, click Save to finalize and create your note.

- Administrator : Full access to all features and settings, able to manage the entire system.
- Technician : Limited access; only able to view or edit items related to specific tasks.
- Estimator : Focused on estimates and financial data without access to other unrelated features.
- Project Manager: Manages the project workflow, including task assignments, but might not need access to financials or settings.Contractor Foreman comes with several preset/default roles to help you get started, but you also have the flexibility to create custom roles to fit the unique structure of your team. Where to find Roles Settings? Roles settings are located in the System Settings of Contractor Foreman. - Administrator : Full access to all features and settings, able to manage the entire system.
- Technician : Limited access; only able to view or edit items related to specific tasks.
- Estimator : Focused on estimates and financial data without access to other unrelated features.
- Project Manager: Manages the project workflow, including task assignments, but might not need access to financials or settings.Contractor Foreman comes with several preset/default roles to help you get started, but you also have the flexibility to create custom roles to fit the unique structure of your team. Where to find Roles Settings? Roles settings are located in the System Settings of Contractor Foreman. Once you are in the Settings module, you will need to access the Roles where roles are created and managed. How to add new roles and modify existing roles.

body:
Roles settings are located in the System Settings of Contractor Foreman. Once you are in the Settings module, you will need to access the Roles where roles are created and managed. How to add new roles and modify existing roles. To add a new role, click the Add Role + button, and then give a name to the role and adjust the permissions of that role in the Edit Screen. To modify existing roles, when you are in the Roles settings, you’ll see a list of existing roles. click the Edit button (represented by a green pencil) to enter modify any role you want to modify, and it will take you to the Edit Screen of the roles. The Edit Screen allows you to modify various aspects of the role:

- Top Section : Here, you can rename the role, change its status (e.g., Active or Inactive), and add any notes or descriptions that clarify the role’s purpose within your team.
- Permissions Section : This section lists every feature and menu item available in Contractor Foreman. For each feature, you can set one of the following access levels:

No Access : The user assigned to this role will not be able to view or interact with the feature. It will be hidden from their view in the menu.

No Access : The user assigned to this role will not be able to view or interact with the feature. It will be hidden from their view in the menu. heading: Default Project
body:
The Default Project is (shown below) is set in the menu bar. Once set, you are telling the system to only show you data that pertains to that project. If you are working the same project for a long period of time, this is a great way to ensure that you are only seeing data for that project.
To assign a Default Project, click on the down arrow and select a project from the list.

To remove the Default Project selection, click on the down arrow and select the currently selected project to unselect it.

title: Assigned Projects & Default Project

heading: Assigned Project(s)
body:
An Assigned Project is a project that your user should be able to see within their account. Often times projects are assigned to supervisors and this allows you to ensure that your supervisor only sees the data that pertains to those projects. It also helps ensure that your sub-contractors only see data for projects they are part of. As an Admin, you should not assign yourself to a project. Too often this is done and then an item such as an Estimate is created and saved and then it appears to vanish. This happens because the Estimate is part of a project that you are not allowed to see/access. The data is there, but your current settings do not allow you to see it.
To add an Assigned Project, go to the Menu > Directory > Users record. Click Edit and then click on Assigned Projects. Click on the project(s) that you want the user to see within Contractor Foreman. Then Save.

To remove an Assigned Project selection, go back to the users Directory record and edit it. Click the Assigned Projects button and then click the projects to unselect them.
NOTE: If you want to see ALL projects, do not select any project in the list.

body: Contractor Foreman provides a powerful Forms and Checklists module that helps you streamline project management with a library of pre-loaded ready-to-use forms and checklists, covering essential areas like safety, inspections, project updates, and more. In addition to using these pre-made templates, you can easily revise or create your own custom forms to fit your specific business needs. It’s important to note that Forms and Checklists in Contractor Foreman can only be filled out by Users (Employees and Contractors that have their own account under your company) in Contractor Foreman. Non-users will not have access to the system to complete these forms digitally, though you can print them out for manual use. When you navigate to the Forms and Checklists module, you will see three widgets on top which show your Recently Submitted Forms, Recent Forms which you’ve created or modified, and your Favorite Forms. Below those widgets, you’ll see a list of forms that are categorized as Used forms and Company forms. Used forms: These are the forms you have used by either assigning a form to someone or by submitting a form.

body:
Below those widgets, you’ll see a list of forms that are categorized as Used forms and Company forms. Used forms: These are the forms you have used by either assigning a form to someone or by submitting a form. Company forms: Once you switch to company forms, you’ll see another filter on the right side called “All” and “Company”.

- All: Here, you will find useful templates that Contractor Foreman offers for you to get started on creating your own company forms. You can use these forms as they are or modify these and save them into your company forms for easy access.
- Company: Any form you’ve customized, or any form you’ve created from scratch, will appear here in company forms.You can use any of the forms either in “All” or in “Company” by clicking the “Use This Form” button to the left of each form. When you click that button, you will be directed to the form where you can fill out the form and submit it, or assign it to someone else so they can fill out the form by logging into their Contractor Foreman account. Also, you can link it to a project if it’s related to a particular project. Despite it is not mandatory, as a best practice we recommend to always select it.

body:

body: The Files and Photos module in Contractor Foreman acts as a centralized library where you can visualize, organize, and manage all the different files that have been uploaded to your account. It serves as a hub for all project-related documents and images, keeping your team aligned and your documentation accessible.
text:
Files and Photos > Basics of Files & Photos

The Files and Photos module in Contractor Foreman acts as a centralized library where you can visualize, organize, and manage all the different files that have been uploaded to your account. It serves as a hub for all project-related documents and images, keeping your team aligned and your documentation accessible.
title: Basics of Files & Photos

heading: Editing Capabilities
body:
Within this module, you can edit different types of files, such as:

- PDFs
- Excel spreadsheets
- Word documents
- ImagesThe Markup feature allows you to:

- Add annotations or comments to your PDFs.
- Fill out predetermined fields on existing PDF forms.
- Edit and work directly on Word and Excel files.Note: These editing features are only available on the desktop version of Contractor Foreman — they are not supported in the mobile app.

heading: Automatic Folder Organization
body:
When you upload files or photos from other modules, Contractor Foreman automatically organizes them into folders within the Files and Photos section.
For example:

- If you upload a photo to a Daily Log for the first time, the system automatically creates a folder named “Daily Logs” under that project.

Every new photo or file uploaded to Daily Logs in that project will now be stored in that same folder.
- The same applies to other modules such as Safety Meetings , Inspections , Incidents , and more.

Upload a file to Safety Meetings for the first time, and a “Safety Meetings” folder will be created automatically.This structure keeps all project files organized by their module of origin.

body: If the labor amounts shown in your Project > Financial > Time Cards section appear lower than expected, it could be due to how wage rates are stored in Contractor Foreman.
text:
Time Cards > My labor amounts are wrong based on hours worked.

If the labor amounts shown in your Project > Financial > Time Cards section appear lower than expected, it could be due to how wage rates are stored in Contractor Foreman.
title: My labor amounts are wrong based on hours worked.

heading: Example Scenario
body:
Let’s say an employee worked 38 hours at $35/hour, so you expect to see $1,330 under Project > Financial > Time Cards.
However, it only shows $210.
text:
Time Cards > My labor amounts are wrong based on hours worked. :: Example Scenario

Let’s say an employee worked 38 hours at $35/hour, so you expect to see $1,330 under Project > Financial > Time Cards.
However, it only shows $210.
title: My labor amounts are wrong based on hours worked.

heading: Why This Happens
body:
When a time card is created, Contractor Foreman stores the wage rate that existed for the employee at the time the card was created.

- These stored rates are not visible in the time card itself — only the system can see them.
- If the time card was created before the wage rate was entered or updated in the Employee Directory , the system uses a default of $0/hour , which leads to incorrect totals.This process is intentional.
If Contractor Foreman always pulled the current wage rate from the Employee Directory, your past records would become inaccurate whenever an employee received a raise.
By storing the rate at the moment of creation, old time cards remain historically accurate.
For example:

- If an employee earned $10/hour last month and now earns $20/hour , old time cards will still reflect the $10 rate — not the new one.

body:
To confirm this is the cause:

- Run a Time Card Report .
- Check the wage rate stored with each time card.
- If older cards were created before wage rates were set or updated, those will show incorrect or lower totals.

- Regulatory compliance : Inspectors often track inspections by specific permit type. If you group them all together, it’s harder to meet local requirements.
- Backtracking and accountability : Having clear categories makes it easy to trace past inspections and permits if questions arise later.

body: In construction, permits and inspections go hand in hand. A permit grants you legal approval to perform certain types of work, while inspections confirm that the work complies with building codes, safety standards, and project specifications. Linking the two in Contractor Foreman ensures that you always maintain a clear, verifiable record.
text:
Permits > What is the reason for linking a permit and an inspection?

In construction, permits and inspections go hand in hand. A permit grants you legal approval to perform certain types of work, while inspections confirm that the work complies with building codes, safety standards, and project specifications. Linking the two in Contractor Foreman ensures that you always maintain a clear, verifiable record.
title: What is the reason for linking a permit and an inspection?

heading: Why link permits and inspections?
body:
- Compliance and accountability A single permit usually requires multiple inspections (e.g., framing, electrical, plumbing, or final inspection). By linking the permit with its inspections, you create a complete record showing that every required step was properly reviewed and passed.
- Paper trail for owners and regulators At the end of a project, you’ll have more than just the permit, you’ll also have documented proof of all inspections tied to it. This provides peace of mind for the owner, builds trust, and ensures you can easily provide evidence if an authority or regulator ever asks.
- Backtracking made easy If an issue comes up months or even years later, you won’t need to dig through separate files. Linked permits and inspections allow you to quickly trace which inspections were completed, by whom, and when.
- Quality assurance Linking ensures nothing is missed. It helps you track progress and confirm that every inspection required under a permit has been performed and documented.

heading: How do I enable or disable Client Portal access?
body:
To disable Client Portal access, go to the Project and click on the Client Portal option located on the left panel at the bottom.

You will see a check box called “Enable Client Access” at right side of the screen. Once this is unchecked, the client portal will be disabled. Right below, there is a drop down called “Preferences”, you will have the ability to set the default settings that apply to all projects by clicking on the option “Save as Default Settings”.

heading: Can I control what my client sees and preview what they will see?
body:
Yes, the client portal can be fully customized and can be previewed.
To preview, go to the Project and click on the Client Access option on the left panel. Once there, click on the “eyeball” icon located on the right side of the screen in between the envelope and “i” icons.
Also, below the Client Access, you will find the “Preferences” drop down and here you can pick and choose what you would like to share with your client. Keep in mind that the “Enable Client Access” box needs to be checked first as the customer you will give access to.

heading: Can my clients create change order request from the Client Portal?
body:
Your clients will have the ability to create a Change Order Request from their client portal account if you have given them permission. Within Project > Settings > Client Access, you will have the ability to set the default settings that apply to all projects. Those defaults are then carried over to the Project record within the Client Access tab. If the box “Create a New CO” is checked, your client will be able to create a new Change Order Request.

They will do so by logging into their Client Portal account and clicking on the Financial tab and clicking the the Submit Change Order button. You will then receive an email notification and the pending CO will be visible in your account for your review.

This means that if you edit the job details, for example, the duration or time frame, the change will automatically apply to all employees assigned to that shift, keeping everything consistent. However, if you need to exclude someone from those updates, you can simply remove that person from the list.

body:

This article explains how to record and manage subcontractor bid numbers received offline (by email, phone, or paper) in Contractor Foreman, along with current limitations and available workarounds.
title: How do I record bid numbers that were given to us offline?

heading: Background
body: While Contractor Foreman allows you to create and manage subcontractor bids, subcontractors currently cannot receive bid requests directly through the system. However, you can still manually record bid numbers and pricing information within the platform to ensure all data stays centralized and easy to track.

heading: 1. Using the Bid Manager (Before Estimate Approval)
body:

- Enter the subcontractor’s bid number and details into the system before the estimate is approved.
- This ensures all bids, including those received offline, are visible and properly stored within the project.

heading: Steps to Review Received Bids
body:
- Go to the Estimates module.
- Select the Bidding section. Within Estimates, click on the Bidding tab to access all active Bid Packages.
- Open the Bid Package you created. Locate and select the specific Bid Package you want to review.
- Click on the Bidders tab. Inside the Bid Package, open the Bidders tab to see all bidders associated with this package.
- Review the new bids. Any new bids received will appear at the bottom of the list. You can open each one to review pricing and details.

First of all, how does a Lead become a Customer within Contractor Foreman?
Converting a Lead to a Customer can be done in a couple of different ways, see below a short list of scenarios.
1. Convert the Lead to a Customer manually.
Go to the Leads Module, once there, find the Lead you would like to convert to a Customer and click on the three-dot-icon “action items”, which will show you the option to “Convert to Customer”.
2. The second way is when there is an Estimate associated to a Lead and then, that Estimate gets “Approved”. Contractor Foreman automatically will convert the Lead to a Customer.
3. The third and last option is when for a reason we create an Invoice to charge a Lead for a service or product done byour company. In this given case, the Lead will become a Customer automatically. Note that the Invoice needs to be on the status submitted.
In any of the above listed scenarios, every data that is present in the Lead will carry over to the Customer record. It is important to note that the Lead will disappear from the Leads Module and it will be found in the Directory Module, on the customer’s profile in the section “files”.

If an email address that you mailed to “bounced”, that means the email server at the other end said that the email address is invalid and does not exists. When that happens, mail can no longer be sent to that address. If you know that the issue has been fixed, you can reactivate the email address so that you can send to it again. To do so, go to the Directory record. Below the email address you will see red text. Click it and it will send a Reactivate request.
If you do not see red text, then there may be some other issue if mail is not being received. In that case, let us know the email address and we can look into it.
text:
Directory & Contacts > An email I sent was not received or bounced.

If an email address that you mailed to “bounced”, that means the email server at the other end said that the email address is invalid and does not exists. When that happens, mail can no longer be sent to that address. If you know that the issue has been fixed, you can reactivate the email address so that you can send to it again. To do so, go to the Directory record. Below the email address you will see red text. Click it and it will send a Reactivate request.
If you do not see red text, then there may be some other issue if mail is not being received. In that case, let us know the email address and we can look into it.
title: An email I sent was not received or bounced.

heading: Overview
body:
In Contractor Foreman, Estimates can include several types of configurable items that define how costs, materials, and customer choices are managed during the bidding and approval process. Understanding the difference between Variations, Options, Allowances, and Selections ensures you create more accurate Estimates and set clear expectations with your clients.
These categories allow you to specify what the customer can choose, what has been pre-selected, and how changes in those choices will affect the total contract amount.
text:
Estimates > What is the difference between Selections, Options, Allowances and Variations? :: Overview

In Contractor Foreman, Estimates can include several types of configurable items that define how costs, materials, and customer choices are managed during the bidding and approval process. Understanding the difference between Variations, Options, Allowances, and Selections ensures you create more accurate Estimates and set clear expectations with your clients.
These categories allow you to specify what the customer can choose, what has been pre-selected, and how changes in those choices will affect the total contract amount.
title: What is the difference between Selections, Options, Allowances and Variations?

heading: Variations
body:
Definition:
Variations are specifications that do not change the price of an item. They are typically details that refine how a particular material or product will be used but do not affect the total cost.
How it Works in Contractor Foreman:

- Variations are added within the CID (Custom Item Details) section as part of a Material item.
- The Contractor Foreman user selects the desired specification before sending the Estimate for approval.Example:

- Paint Colour: The material (paint) is already priced in the Estimate, and the user simply selects the colour (e.g., “Cloud White” or “Warm Beige”) without changing the cost.
- Roofing Shingle Type: The type or style of shingle (e.g., “Architectural” vs. “Three-Tab”) is chosen, but the price remains the same.

title: What is the difference between Selections, Options, Allowances and Variations?

heading: Options
body:
Definition:
Options are specifications where the customer chooses between two or more alternative items, each with its own price. When the customer selects an optional item, the price of that item is added to the Estimate.
How it Works in Contractor Foreman:

- Options can apply to Material , Labour , Equipment , Subcontractor , or Other items.
- Each item is listed in the Estimate with its corresponding cost.
- When the Estimate is submitted for approval , the customer reviews the available options and makes a selection electronically.Example:

- Countertops: The Estimate might include both “Granite Counter ($4,500)” and “Laminate Counter ($2,000).”
- The customer chooses the preferred option during the approval stage.
- The selected item is then added to the final contract price.

heading: Allowances
body:
Definition:
Allowances represent budgeted amounts included in the Estimate for specific items that the customer will later choose. The allowance amount forms part of the Estimate total and indicates how much has been allocated for that particular item.
How it Works in Contractor Foreman:

- The builder includes an allowance line item in the Estimate (e.g., “Bathroom Vanity Allowance – $6,000”).
- This lets the customer know how much is available to spend on that item.
- If the customer chooses an item that costs more than the allowance, a Change Order is issued to account for the price difference.Example:

- The Estimate includes a $6,000 allowance for a bathroom vanity.
- The customer later chooses a vanity worth $7,000 .
- The builder issues a Change Order for $1,000 to cover the difference.

heading: Selections
body:
Definition:
Selections are items that the customer must decide on during the bidding or estimating process. Once the customer makes their selection, the associated price is added to the Estimate.
How it Works in Contractor Foreman:

- The Estimate may initially include a placeholder item with a cost of $0 , indicating a pending customer choice.
- Once the customer selects the desired item or specification, the builder updates the Estimate with the actual price.
- After the Estimate is approved and converted into a Project , any further changes are handled through Change Orders .Example:

- An item called “Flooring” is listed at $0 in the Estimate.
- The customer later chooses hardwood flooring for $8,500 , and that cost is added to the Estimate.
- Any future flooring changes (e.g., switching to tile) are handled through a Change Order.

heading: Best Practices
body:
- Clearly distinguish between Variations and Options to avoid confusion during client approval.
- Always include Allowances for major client-driven items to maintain pricing transparency.
- Document all Selections and follow up promptly to prevent project delays.
- Use Change Orders for any price differences arising after project approval.
- Ensure all client choices are updated in the Estimate before converting it to a Project.

body: To set up and add a VAT Reverse Charge (or Reverse Tax) in Contractor Foreman, first, go to the Main Menu of Contractor Foreman. From here, navigate to Settings, and go to the Financial Settings. Scroll down to find the setting field called Tax Rates. This section is where you manage all your tax rates, including creating new ones and setting up reverse charges. You will see a button labeled Add Tax Rate +. Click this to start the process of creating a new tax rate. On the next screen, you’ll have options to configure the tax rate. You will need to enter the details for the new tax rate you want to create. Start by providing a name for the tax, and then you can select whether you are setting up a Single Tax or a Multi-Tax item. This option allows flexibility depending on how the tax is structured in your region. Below the tax name, you will see a checkbox labeled Tax is Reversible. Check this box if you are setting up a Tax Reverse. If the box is selected, the tax will be applied to the Invoice or Estimate and then deducted, causing the Total to match the Subtotal. Additionaly, enter the percentage of the tax and make sure to review the fields carefully and save changes.

In Contractor Foreman, both Attachments and Associated Files appear as sections within the Daily Logs module. While they may look similar, the difference lies in where the files were originally uploaded.
title: Attachments vs Associated Files: What is the difference?

heading: Attachments
body:
Attachments are files that are uploaded directly to the Daily Log.
These can include photos, documents, or any other files added manually while creating or editing the Daily Log.
Example:
If you upload jobsite photos or inspection reports directly in the Daily Log, those files are considered Attachments.

heading: Associated Files
body:
Associated Files are files that were uploaded in other modules, such as the Project module or Safety Meetings, on the same day the Daily Log was created.
The Daily Log automatically pulls in and displays those files as Associated Files, allowing you to view all related documentation from the same day in one place.
Example:
If a document or image was uploaded to the Project or Safety Meetings module on the same date, that file will appear in the Daily Log under the Associated Files section.

A Work in Progress or WIP report is used by a contractor and its accounting staff to correctly recognize the Revenue being generated by that specific project and “balance” the amount of billings being posted so as not to overstate or understate income for the accounting period. You begin by identifying 4 current values at the time the report is being run.

- Current Contract Value , defined as the Original Contract Value signed by the customer, and adding any Approved Change Orders and Work Orders for work added after the contract is signed.
- Current Billings , defined as the total amount of Invoices the contractor has submitted to the customer.
- Current Cost Budget , defined as the Estimated Cost of the Original Contract plus Estimated Cost of Approved Change Orders and Work Orders.
- Total Actual Costs , defined as the total of all Timecards, Expenses, and Bills posted to the Project to date.Revenue for a construction project is recognized based on a Percent Complete basis.

- % complete as submitted by a Project Manager who has a good feel for how far the project has progressed.Within the Contractor Foreman Work in Progress report, we calculate the Cost % Complete as this is the least subjective, and is defined as (Total Actual Costs divided by the Current Cost Budget). Next we display the Forecasted % Complete, which will be used in the final calculations on the report. If there is a Schedule being used for this project in Contractor Foreman, that % will be displayed in the report. The Forecasted Complete value is based on either the overall progress of tasks in the Project Schedule or the % complete entered manually in the Work in Progress section of the Project Details. Earned Revenue is then calculated by multiplying the (Forecasted % Complete by the Current Contract Value), thereby establishing how much Revenue is “Earned” based on how close the project is to being completed.

body: Earned Revenue is then calculated by multiplying the (Forecasted % Complete by the Current Contract Value), thereby establishing how much Revenue is “Earned” based on how close the project is to being completed. Earned Revenue is then compared to the Current Billings submitted, and if Current Billings is larger than Earned Revenue, the difference is entered in the Over Billings column. If Current Billings is smaller than Earned Revenue, the difference is entered in the Under Billings column. Each month the accounting staff runs this report and makes an adjusting entry to their Income Statement to reflect the proper values for their active projects. Then next month they reverse that entry, run the report(s) and make that month’s adjusting entry. The significance of this report and its use is very important to Bonding Companies and Banks, who want to see that each project is properly “balanced” and the contractor is not using dollars from one or two projects to finance other projects. The contractor, likewise does not want to be internally financing his active jobs by significantly underbilling them.

heading: Compliance Notice vs. Schedule Notice
body: Contractor Foreman provides two types of prebuilt notice forms commonly used for formal construction correspondence: Compliance Notices and Schedule Notices. While both forms help document issues and communicate expectations with subcontractors, vendors, or project partners, each serves a different purpose in project management.
text:
RFI & Notices > Compliance Notice vs Schedule Notice :: Compliance Notice vs. Schedule Notice

Contractor Foreman provides two types of prebuilt notice forms commonly used for formal construction correspondence: Compliance Notices and Schedule Notices. While both forms help document issues and communicate expectations with subcontractors, vendors, or project partners, each serves a different purpose in project management.
title: Compliance Notice vs Schedule Notice

heading: Purpose
body: A Compliance Notice is used to formally notify a subcontractor or vendor that their work is not meeting contractual requirements, specifications, or expectations. This notice creates a documented record of performance issues and allows the responsible party an opportunity to correct the problem before further action—such as a back charge or a negative Change Order—is taken.
text:
RFI & Notices > Compliance Notice vs Schedule Notice :: Purpose

A Compliance Notice is used to formally notify a subcontractor or vendor that their work is not meeting contractual requirements, specifications, or expectations. This notice creates a documented record of performance issues and allows the responsible party an opportunity to correct the problem before further action—such as a back charge or a negative Change Order—is taken.
title: Compliance Notice vs Schedule Notice

heading: When to Use
body:
A Compliance Notice should be issued when work is:

- Out of Scope
- Out of Compliance with plans or specifications
- Completed with Poor Workmanship
- Not Meeting Contract Requirements
- Any other issue that needs to be addressed (labeled as Other )Contractor Foreman includes five types of Compliance Notices:

- Out of Scope Work
- Out of Compliance Work
- Poor Workmanship
- Not Meeting Contract Requirements
- Other

heading: Example Scenario
body: A subcontractor installs interior trim and stain, but the stain is uneven and blotchy. You verbally request a fix, but they refuse. You send a Compliance Notice with the type “Poor Workmanship”, documenting the issue and giving them a deadline to correct it. If the subcontractor still refuses, this notice supports issuing a back charge or negative Change Order.

The Gantt chart provided within Contractor Foreman is a great way for you to schedule tasks based on resource availability. When adding a Task to a Schedule, you will have the option to designate an Assigned Contractor and and Employee. Assigned Contractor: This is the person that is doing the work. It can be anyone from within your Contractor Foreman directory, including; Contractors, Vendors, Customers, etc. Employee: This is the team member that is overseeing the task or that needs to be associated with the tasks. Examples of how this may be used are:

- A plumbing inspection is scheduled for next Wednesday. The Assigned Contractor would be the plumber and the Employee would be either the Superintendent/ Project Manager so both parties (the sub and the PM) show up to meet the county official.
- An invoice needs to be created on the 25th of the month. Assigned Contractor might be the Accounting Staff member and the Employee would be the PM for approval.
- Roof shingles are being delivered on Monday. Sub is Assigned Contractor so they can begin installation and coordinate with the supply house where they want the shingles placed.
